2.1.m:
Veṅkaṭācalamāhātmya.
Nārada's vision of Yajñavarāha on the summit of Sumeru.
In the holy Naimiṣāraṇya, Śaunaka and the other great seers / performed a twelve-year sacrificial session for the protection of the world. // 1
To them came the story-teller, the pupil of Vyāsa of great intellect, / the sage named Ugraśravas, born of Romaharṣaṇa. // 2
Being duly worshipped by them, Sūta, the best of Purāṇa reciters, / narrated that divine Purāṇa named Skanda. // 3
He related in detail the story of the creation, dissolution, and lineages, / of the deeds of the dynasties, and of the manvantaras. // 4
Having heard the stories of the powers of the sacred fords, those foremost of sages / spoke to the self-controlled Sūta, eager to hear [more] stories. // 5
The seers said:
"O Romaharṣaṇa, all-knowing one, skilled in the meaning of the Purāṇas! / We wish to hear the māhātmya of the great mountains on earth. / Tell us, O fortunate one, which are the foremost mountains?" // 6
Śrī Sūta said:
"Formerly, on the bank of the Ganges, I asked this very question / to Vyāsa, the foremost of great sages; that best of teachers spoke to me." // 7
Vyāsa said:
"Formerly, in the age of the gods, O Sūta, Nārada, the best of sages, / having gone to the summit of Sumeru, shining with various jewels, // 8
and having seen in its center the vast, radiant, divine abode of Brahmā, / saw to its north an excellent pippala tree, // 9
a thousand yojanas high and twice as broad. / At its base was a divine pavilion, adorned with various gems, // 10
adorned with thousands of ruby pillars, / with rows of auspicious emblems made of beryl and pearls, // 11
strown with the nine jewels, beautified by divine archways, / filled with auspicious beasts and birds made of the nine jewels, // 12
having a great gate of topaz, a gateway tower of seven storeys, / beautified by two doors well-fashioned from radiant diamonds. // 13

2.1.m:
Having entered, he saw within a divine pavilion of pearls;
the great sage ascended a lofty platform of beryl. // 14
In its center, lofty, peerless, adorned with eight legs,
he saw a throne covered with pearls, of great splendor. // 15
In its center was a divine lotus, adorned with a thousand petals,
white, lustrous as a thousand moons, bright with pericarp and filaments. // 16
Seated in its center, with the brilliance of ten thousand full moons,
having the form of Mount Kailāsa, handsome, having a human form, // 17
four-armed, with noble limbs, an auspicious boar-face,
bearing the conch, discus, and gestures of granting safety and boons, the Supreme Person, // 18
the god wearing yellow garments, with eyes long like lotus petals,
with a gentle face like the full moon, his lotus mouth fragrant with incense, // 19
sounding with the Sāma Veda, the embodiment of sacrifice, with a snout like a offering ladle and a nose like a sacrificial spoon,
resembling the ocean of milk, with his face radiant with a diadem, // 20
with the śrīvatsa mark on his chest, adorned with a bright sacred thread,
blazing with the splendor of the Kaustubha gem, having an elevated, broad chest, // 21

2.1.m:
endowed with divine ornaments of excellent jewels made of gold,
radiant like an autumn cloud encircled by garlands of lightning, // 22
splendid on a footstool pressed by the sole of his left foot,
ever brilliant with bracelets, armlets, upper-arm bands, and earrings, // 23
by the four-faced [Brahmā], Vasiṣṭha, Atri, Mārkaṇḍeya, and other lords of sages,
and by Bhṛgu and many others, served day and night, // 24
and by the world-guardians headed by Indra, and hosts of gandharvas and apsarases—
having approached and bowed down to that God of gods thus served, // 25
and having praised the Supporter of the Earth with divine passages from the Upaniṣads,
Nārada, exceedingly pleased, stood in the presence of the god. // 26
Now the arrival of Dharaṇī before Varāha.
In the meantime, there arose the sound of divine kettledrums. // 27
Then goddess Dharaṇī came there together with her companions,
radiant in divine garments resembling an ocean of excellent jewels, // 28
bent low under the weight of breasts shaped like Sumeru and Mandara,
dark as fresh dūrvā grass blades, adorned with all ornaments, // 29

2.1.m:
accompanied indeed by her two friends Ilā and Piṅgalā.
Then, scattering at the feet of the glorious god Varāha
the heap of flowers brought by those two, the Earth, // 30
having bowed to the God of gods, stood with joined palms. // 31
Then the glorious Varāha, having embraced that goddess and placed her on his lap, // 32
Now the dialogue of Dharaṇī and Varāha.
asked the Earth about her welfare, his mind disposed to affection. // 33
Glorious Varāha said:
"Having placed you, O goddess Earth, upon the comfortable head of Śeṣa,
and having established the world upon you, and mountains as your helpers,
I have come here, O goddess. For what purpose have you come here?" // 34
The Earth said:
"Having lifted me up from Pātāla onto the lofty, jeweled head of Ananta,
adorned with a thousand hoods, as if onto a jewel-seat,
and having made me firmly fixed, O god, and having established the mountains // 35
capable of bearing me, holy, identical with you, O Supreme Person,
tell me of the foremost among them, O mighty-armed one, that are my supports." // 36

मेरुपुत्रोऽञ्जनो नाम शैलः स्वर्णमयो महान् .. 38 ..
एते शैलवराः सर्वे त्वदाधारा वसुन्धरे ..
ये मया देवसंघैश्च ऋषिसंघैश्च सेविताः ..39..
एतेषु प्रवरान्वक्ष्ये तत्त्वतः शृणु माधवि ..
सालग्रामश्च सिंहाद्रिश्शैलेंद्रो गन्धमादनः.. ..2.1.1.40..
एते शैलवरा देवि दिशं हैमवतीं श्रिताः ..
दक्षिणस्यां प्रतीतांस्तु वक्ष्ये शैलान्वसुन्धरे ..41..
अरुणाद्रिर्हस्तिशैलो गृध्राद्रिर्घटिकाचलः ..
एते शैलवराः सर्वे क्षीरनद्यास्समीपगाः .. 42..
हस्तिशैलादुत्तरतः पंचयोजनमात्रतः ..
सुवर्णमुखरीनाम नदीनां प्रवरा नदी .. 43 ..
2.1.m:
Now the description of Śeṣācala surpassing all mountains.
Glorious Varāha said:
"Sumeru, Himavat, Vindhya, Mandara, Gandhamādana,
Sālagrāma, Citrakūṭa, Mālyavat, Pāriyātra, // 37
Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Siṃhādri, and Raivata,
and the great golden mountain named Añjana, the son of Meru— // 38
all these excellent mountains are your supports, O Vasundharā,
which are frequented by me, and by hosts of gods, and by hosts of seers. // 39
Among these I will declare the foremost in truth; listen, O Mādhavī:
Sālagrāma, Siṃhādri, and Gandhamādana, the king of mountains..." // 40
These best of mountains, O goddess, are situated in the northern direction;
now I shall describe the famous mountains in the south, O Vasundharā: // 41
Aruṇādri, Hastiśaila, Gṛdhrādri, Ghaṭikācala—
all these best of mountains stand near the Kṣīranadī. // 42
To the north of Hastiśaila, at a distance of five yojanas,
flows the foremost of rivers, named Suvarṇamukharī. // 43

2.1.s:
tasyā evottare tīre kamalākhyaṃ sarovaram ..
tattīre bhagavānāste śukasya varado hariḥ..44..
balabhadreṇa saṃyuktaḥ kṛṣṇo bhaktārtināśanaḥ..
vaikhānasairmunigaṇairnityamārādhito'malaiḥ .45..
kamalākhyasya sarasa uttare kānanottame ..
krośadvayārdhamātre tu haricaṃdanaśobhite ..
śrīveṃkaṭācalonāma vāsudevālayo mahān ...46..
saptayojanavistīrṇaḥ śailendro yojanocchritaḥ ..
asti svarṇamayo devi ratnasānubhṛdāyataḥ ..47..
indrādyā daivatagaṇā vasiṣṭhādyā munīśvarāḥ..
siddhāḥ sādhyāśca maruto dānavā daityarākṣasāḥ ..
rambhādyā apsaraḥsaṃghā vasanti niyataṃ dhare .. 40 ..
tapaścaraṃti nāgāśca garuḍāḥ kinnarāstathā ..
etairadhiṣṭhitāstatra saritaḥ puṇyadarśanāḥ ..
sarāṃsi vividhānyatra saṃti divyāni mādhavi .. 49 ..
.. atha svāmipuṣkariṇyāḥ sarvatīrthātiśāyitvavarṇanam .. ..
2.1.d:
तस्या एवोत्तरे तीरे कमलाख्यं सरोवरम् ..
तत्तीरे भगवानास्ते शुकस्य वरदो हरिः..44..
बलभद्रेण संयुक्तः कृष्णो भक्तार्तिनाशनः..
वैखानसैर्मुनिगणैर्नित्यमाराधितोऽमलैः .45..
कमलाख्यस्य सरस उत्तरे काननोत्तमे ..
क्रोशद्वयार्धमात्रे तु हरिचंदनशोभिते ..
श्रीवेंकटाचलोनाम वासुदेवालयो महान् ...46..
सप्तयोजनविस्तीर्णः शैलेन्द्रो योजनोच्छ्रितः ..
अस्ति स्वर्णमयो देवि रत्नसानुभृदायतः ..47..
इन्द्राद्या दैवतगणा वसिष्ठाद्या मुनीश्वराः..
सिद्धाः साध्याश्च मरुतो दानवा दैत्यराक्षसाः ..
रम्भाद्या अप्सरःसंघा वसन्ति नियतं धरे .. 40 ..
तपश्चरंति नागाश्च गरुडाः किन्नरास्तथा ..
एतैरधिष्ठितास्तत्र सरितः पुण्यदर्शनाः ..
सरांसि विविधान्यत्र संति दिव्यानि माधवि .. 49 ..
.. अथ स्वामिपुष्करिण्याः सर्वतीर्थातिशायित्ववर्णनम् .. ..
2.1.m:
On its northern bank is a lake called Kamala;
on its shore dwells the blessed lord Hari, granter of boons to Śuka, // 44
joined by Balabhadra—Kṛṣṇa, who destroys the distress of his devotees,
perpetually worshipped by the immaculate hosts of Vaikhānasa sages. // 45
To the north of Lake Kamala, in an excellent forest,
at a distance of just two and a half krośas, adorned with yellow-sandal trees,
is the great abode of Vāsudeva named Śrīveṅkaṭācala. // 46
Seven yojanas in breadth, one yojana high,
this lord of mountains is golden, O goddess, possessing peaks of jewels and extending far. // 47
Hosts of gods beginning with Indra, lords of sages beginning with Vasiṣṭha,
Siddhas, Sādhyas, and Maruts, Dānavas, Daityas, and Rākṣasas,
and troops of apsarases beginning with Rambhā dwell there constantly, O earth; // 48
Nāgas, Garuḍas, and Kinnaras perform austerity there.
Occupied by these, sacred-looking rivers are there,
and various divine lakes exist here, O Mādhavī. // 49
Now the description of the superiority of Svāmipuṣkariṇī over all sacred fords.

2.1.s:
tīrthānāṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ śṛṇuṣva pravarāṇi vai ..2.1.1.50..
cakratīrthaṃ daivatīrthaṃ viyadgaṃgā tathaiva ca ..
kumāradhārikātīrthaṃ pāpanāśanameva ca ..
pāṇḍavaṃ nāma tīrthaṃ ca svāmipuṣkariṇī tathā .. 51 ..
saptaitāni varāṇyāhurnārāyaṇagirau śubhe ..
eteṣu pravarā devi svāmipuṣkariṇī śubhā .. 52 ..
asyāstu paścime tīraṃ nivasāmi tvayā saha ..
āste'syā dakṣiṇe tīraṃ śrīnivāso jagatpatiḥ .. 53 ..
gaṃgādyaiḥ sakalaistīrthaiḥ samā sā sāgarāmbare ..
trailokye yāni tīrthāni sarāṃsi saritastathā ..
teṣāṃ svāmitvamāpannaṃ dhare svāmisarovare .. 54 ..
svāmipuṣkariṇīṃ puṇyāṃ sevituṃ divyabhūdhare ..
vasanti sarvatīrthāni teṣāṃ saṃkhyāṃ vadāmi te .. 55 ..
ṣaṭṣaṣṭikoṭitīrthāni puṇye'sminbhūdharottame ..
teṣu cātyaṃtamukhyāni ṣaṭ tīrthāni vasundhare .. 56 ..
2.1.d:
तीर्थानां चैव सर्वेषां शृणुष्व प्रवराणि वै ..2.1.1.50..
चक्रतीर्थं दैवतीर्थं वियद्गंगा तथैव च ..
कुमारधारिकातीर्थं पापनाशनमेव च ..
पाण्डवं नाम तीर्थं च स्वामिपुष्करिणी तथा .. 51 ..
सप्तैतानि वराण्याहुर्नारायणगिरौ शुभे ..
एतेषु प्रवरा देवि स्वामिपुष्करिणी शुभा .. 52 ..
अस्यास्तु पश्चिमे तीरं निवसामि त्वया सह ..
आस्तेऽस्या दक्षिणे तीरं श्रीनिवासो जगत्पतिः .. 53 ..
गंगाद्यैः सकलैस्तीर्थैः समा सा सागराम्बरे ..
त्रैलोक्ये यानि तीर्थानि सरांसि सरितस्तथा ..
तेषां स्वामित्वमापन्नं धरे स्वामिसरोवरे .. 54 ..
स्वामिपुष्करिणीं पुण्यां सेवितुं दिव्यभूधरे ..
वसन्ति सर्वतीर्थानि तेषां संख्यां वदामि ते .. 55 ..
षट्षष्टिकोटितीर्थानि पुण्येऽस्मिन्भूधरोत्तमे ..
तेषु चात्यंतमुख्यानि षट् तीर्थानि वसुन्धरे .. 56 ..
2.1.m:
Hear indeed the foremost among all the sacred fords: // 50
Cakratīrtha, Daivatīrtha, and likewise Viyadgaṅgā,
Kumāradhārikātīrtha, and Pāpanāśana,
the sacred ford named Pāṇḍava, and likewise Svāmipuṣkariṇī— // 51
these seven, they say, are the best on the auspicious Nārāyaṇagiri.
Foremost among these, O goddess, is the auspicious Svāmipuṣkariṇī. // 52
On its western bank I reside together with you;
on its southern bank dwells Śrīnivāsa, the lord of the world. // 53
Equal to all sacred fords including the Gaṅgā is that lake, O earth ocean-clad;
whatever sacred fords, lakes, and rivers there are in the three worlds,
lordship over them has accrued to the Svāmisarovara, O earth. // 54
To serve the holy Svāmipuṣkariṇī on this divine mountain,
all the sacred fords reside; I shall tell you their number: // 55
there are sixty-six crores of sacred fords on this sacred, best of mountains;
and among them, six sacred fords are paramount, O Vasundharā. // 56

2.1.s:
pañcānāṃ tīrtharājānāṃ tumbo garbhasamo mahān ..
garbhavāsabhayadhvaṃsī snātānāṃ bhūdharottame .. 57 ..
.. dharaṇyuvāca .. ..
ṣaṭ tīrthāni mahābāho tvayoktāni mahīdhare ..
māhātmyaṃ vada teṣāṃ me yathākālaṃ yathāvidhi ..
phalāni teṣu snātānāṃ narāṇāṃ vada bhūdhara .. 58 .. ..
.. śrīvarāha uvāca .. ..
nārāyaṇādrimāhātmyaṃ vadāmi śṛṇu mādhavi .. 59 ..
devāśca ṛṣayaścaiva yoginaḥ sanakādayaḥ ..
kṛteṃ'janādriṃ tretāyāṃ nārāyaṇagiriṃ tathā .. 2.1.1.60 ..
dvāpare siṃhaśailaṃ ca kalau śrīveṅkaṭācalam ..
pravadantīha vidvāṃsaḥ paramātmālayaṃ girim .. 61 ..
yojanānāṃ sahasrānte dvīpāṃtaragato'pi vā ..
yo namedbhūdharendraṃ taddiśamuddiśya bhaktitaḥ ..
sarvapāpavinirmukto viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati .. 62 ..
tasminṣaṭtīrthamāhātmyaṃ yathākālaṃ vadāmi te .. 63 ..
.. atha kumāradhārāmāhātmyam .. ..
2.1.d:
पञ्चानां तीर्थराजानां तुम्बो गर्भसमो महान् ..
गर्भवासभयध्वंसी स्नातानां भूधरोत्तमे .. 57 ..
.. धरण्युवाच .. ..
षट् तीर्थानि महाबाहो त्वयोक्तानि महीधरे ..
माहात्म्यं वद तेषां मे यथाकालं यथाविधि ..
फलानि तेषु स्नातानां नराणां वद भूधर .. 58 .. ..
.. श्रीवराह उवाच .. ..
नारायणाद्रिमाहात्म्यं वदामि शृणु माधवि .. 59 ..
देवाश्च ऋषयश्चैव योगिनः सनकादयः ..
कृतेंऽजनाद्रिं त्रेतायां नारायणगिरिं तथा .. 2.1.1.60 ..
द्वापरे सिंहशैलं च कलौ श्रीवेङ्कटाचलम् ..
प्रवदन्तीह विद्वांसः परमात्मालयं गिरिम् .. 61 ..
योजनानां सहस्रान्ते द्वीपांतरगतोऽपि वा ..
यो नमेद्भूधरेन्द्रं तद्दिशमुद्दिश्य भक्तितः ..
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो विष्णुलोकं स गच्छति .. 62 ..
तस्मिन्षट्तीर्थमाहात्म्यं यथाकालं वदामि ते .. 63 ..
.. अथ कुमारधारामाहात्म्यम् .. ..
2.1.m:
Among five kingly fords, the great Tumba is like a womb;
it destroys the fear of entering the womb for those who bathe [there] on this best of mountains. // 57
Dharaṇī said:
Six sacred fords on the mountain have been mentioned by you, O mighty-armed one;
tell me their māhātmya, along with the proper time and the proper injunction,
and tell [me] the fruits for men who bathe in them, O maintainer of the earth. // 58
The glorious Varāha said:
I shall tell the māhātmya of Nārāyaṇādri; hear, O Mādhavī: // 59
gods, seers, and yogins beginning with Sanaka,
and wise men declare this mountain to be the abode of the Supreme Self—
as Añjanādri in the Kṛta age, Nārāyaṇagiri in the Tretā age, / Siṃhaśaila in the Dvāpara, and Śrīveṅkaṭācala in the Kali age. // 60–61
The wise here declare that mountain to be the abode of the Supreme Self.
Even one stationed at the end of a thousand yojanas or gone to another continent,
who bows in devotion facing in the direction of this lord of mountains,
is freed from all sins and goes to the world of Viṣṇu. // 62
I will describe to you the māhātmya of the six sacred fords there, according to the proper time. // 63
Now the māhātmya of Kumāradhārā.

2.1.s:
śṛṇuṣvāvahitā bhadre sarvapāpapraṇāśanam ..
kubhasaṃsthe ravau māghe paurṇamāsyāṃ mahātithau .. 64 ..
maghānakṣatrayuktāyāṃ bhūdharendre vasundhare ..
kumāradhārikānāma sarasī lokapāvanī .. 65 ..
yatrāste pārvatīsūnuḥ kārtikeyo'gnisaṃbhavaḥ ..
devasenāsamāyuktaḥ śrīnivāsārcako'male .. 66 ..
tasyāṃ yaḥ snāti madhyāhne tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu ..
gaṃgādisarvatīrtheṣu yaḥ snāti niyamāddharaṃ ..
dvādaśābdaṃ jagaddhātri tatphalaṃ samavāpnuyāt .. 67 ..
yo'nnaṃ dadāti tattīrthe śaktyā dakṣiṇayānvitam ..
sa tāvatphalamāpnoti snāne tūktaṃ phalaṃ yathā .. 68 ..
.. atha tuṃbatīrthamāhātmyam .. ..
mānasaṃsthe savitari paurṇamāsītithau dhare ..
uttarāphālgunīyukte caturthe kāla uttame .. 69 ..
paṃcānāmapi tīrthānāṃ tuṃbe'tha girigahvare ..
yaḥ snāti manujo devi punargarbhe na jāyate .. 2.1.1.70 ..
2.1.d:
शृणुष्वावहिता भद्रे सर्वपापप्रणाशनम् ..
कुभसंस्थे रवौ माघे पौर्णमास्यां महातिथौ .. 64 ..
मघानक्षत्रयुक्तायां भूधरेन्द्रे वसुन्धरे ..
कुमारधारिकानाम सरसी लोकपावनी .. 65 ..
यत्रास्ते पार्वतीसूनुः कार्तिकेयोऽग्निसंभवः ..
देवसेनासमायुक्तः श्रीनिवासार्चकोऽमले .. 66 ..
तस्यां यः स्नाति मध्याह्ने तस्य पुण्यफलं शृणु ..
गंगादिसर्वतीर्थेषु यः स्नाति नियमाद्धरं ..
द्वादशाब्दं जगद्धात्रि तत्फलं समवाप्नुयात् .. 67 ..
योऽन्नं ददाति तत्तीर्थे शक्त्या दक्षिणयान्वितम् ..
स तावत्फलमाप्नोति स्नाने तूक्तं फलं यथा .. 68 ..
.. अथ तुंबतीर्थमाहात्म्यम् .. ..
मानसंस्थे सवितरि पौर्णमासीतिथौ धरे ..
उत्तराफाल्गुनीयुक्ते चतुर्थे काल उत्तमे .. 69 ..
पंचानामपि तीर्थानां तुंबेऽथ गिरिगह्वरे ..
यः स्नाति मनुजो देवि पुनर्गर्भे न जायते .. 2.1.1.70 ..
2.1.m:
Listen attentively, O auspicious one, [to what] destroys all sins:
when the sun resides in Aquarius, in the month of Māgha, on the great lunar day of the full moon, // 64
joined with the Maghā asterism, on this lord of mountains, O Vasundharā,
there is a pool named Kumāradhārikā that purifies the world, // 65
where dwells Pārvatī's son, Kārttikeya, who was born from fire,
joined with Devasenā, worshipping Śrīnivāsa, O pure one. // 66
Hear the fruit of merit of one who bathes in it at midday:
One who bathes with regularity in all sacred fords such as the Gaṅgā, O Earth,
for twelve years, O supporter of the world, obtains that very fruit.
One who gives food at that sacred ford according to one's capacity, accompanied by a fee,
reaps that same fruit, just as the fruit has been described for the ritual ablution.
Now, the māhātmya of the Tumba sacred ford.
When the sun is stationed in the Mānasa, on the full moon day, O Earth,
conjoined with Uttarāphālgunī, at the fourth auspicious period,
among the five sacred fords, then at Tumba in the mountain cave,
the person who bathes, O goddess, is not born into a womb again.

2.1.s:
atha ākāśagaṃgāmāhātmyam ..
agnivāhasthite bhānau citrānakṣatrasaṃyute ..
pūrṇimākhye tithau puṇye prātaḥkāle tathaiva ca ..
ākāśagaṃgāsariti snāto mokṣamavāpnuyāt .. 71 ..
.. atha pāṇḍavatīrthamāhātmyam .. ..
vṛṣabhasthe ravau rādhe dvādaśyāṃ ravivāsare ..
śukle vāpyatha vā kṛṣṇe pakṣe bhaumasamanvite .. 72 ..
śukle vāpyathavā kṛṣṇe bhānuvāreṇa saṃyute ..
puṣyanakṣatrasaṃyukta hastarkṣeṇa yute'pi vā .. 73 ..
tīrthe pāṃḍavanāmnyatra saṃgave snāti yo naraḥ ..
neha duḥkhamavāpnoti paratra sukhamaśnute .. 74 ..
atha pāpanāśanatīrthamāhātmyam ..
śukle pakṣe'tha vā kṛṣṇe yārkavāreṇa saptamī ..
puṣyanakṣatrasaṃyuktā hastarkṣeṇa yutāpi vā .. 75 ..
tasyāṃ tithau mahābhāge pāpanāśanasaṃjñake ..
tīrthe yaḥ snāti niyamādbhūdharendrasya mastake .. 76 ..
2.1.d:
अथ आकाशगंगामाहात्म्यम् ..
अग्निवाहस्थिते भानौ चित्रानक्षत्रसंयुते ..
पूर्णिमाख्ये तिथौ पुण्ये प्रातःकाले तथैव च ..
आकाशगंगासरिति स्नातो मोक्षमवाप्नुयात् .. 71 ..
.. अथ पाण्डवतीर्थमाहात्म्यम् .. ..
वृषभस्थे रवौ राधे द्वादश्यां रविवासरे ..

2.1.m:
Now, the māhātmya of Ākāśagaṅgā.
When the sun is in the constellation of Agnivāha, conjoined with the Citrā nakṣatra,
on the holy lunar day called the full moon, and likewise at dawn,
having bathed in the river Ākāśagaṅgā, one attains liberation.
Now, the māhātmya of the Pāṇḍava sacred ford.
When the sun is in Taurus, in the month of Vaiśākha, on the twelfth lunar day, on a Sunday,
whether in the bright or dark fortnight, conjoined with Tuesday;
or in the bright or dark [fortnight] conjoined with Sunday,
or conjoined with the Puṣya nakṣatra or conjoined with the Hasta constellation:
the person who bathes here at the sacred ford named Pāṇḍava at morning-time
incurs no suffering in this world, and enjoys happiness in the next.
Now, the māhātmya of the Pāpanāśana sacred ford.
In the bright or dark fortnight, a seventh lunar day falling on Sunday,
conjoined with the Puṣya nakṣatra or conjoined with the Hasta constellation:
on that lunar day, O fortunate one, in the one named Pāpanāśana,
the sacred ford on the summit of the king of mountains, one who bathes with regularity

Now, the māhātmya of the Deva sacred ford.
Hear the supreme secret, O goddess, on the great mountain named Ananta:
to the northwest of my divine abode, on the peak, in a mountain cave,
is an exceedingly beautiful pool known as the Deva sacred ford.
I shall tell you the time for ritual ablution in that most holy [place], O goddess:
when Puṣya falls on a Thursday, at a Vyatīpāta, and likewise when Śravaṇa falls on a Monday—
hear the fruit of merit of one who bathes on these days:
Whatever sins are committed here through knowledge or ignorance,
all of them are destroyed at the exceedingly purifying Deva sacred ford.
Merits also increase from bathing in the Deva sacred ford;
one attains a long life, accompanied by sons and grandsons,
and at the end, having reached heaven, is exalted in Candraloka.
The giver of food on those days, O goddess, becomes [equivalent to] a giver of food for life.
This most secret [truth], O goddess, has been declared to you, O Earth.

Now, the praise of Varāha by Earth.
Earth said:
Obeisance to you, O Lord of the gods of gods, O boar-faced, unswerving one,
resembling the ocean of milk, diamond-tusked, mighty-armed!
I was lifted up by you, O God, from the waters of the ocean at the beginning of the kalpa;
by you of a thousand arms, O Viṣṇu, I uphold the worlds.
You who are adorned with various divine ornaments and the sacred thread,
wearing deep red garments, embellished with divine gems,
whose lotus feet resemble the rising sun, obeisance, obeisance [to you]!
The tip of whose tusks gleams like the crescent moon, O you of great power and valor,
whose limbs are anointed with divine sandalwood, wearing earrings of refined gold,
adorned with golden armlets gleaming with sapphire gems,
who tore asunder Hiraṇyākṣa with the tip of your diamond tusk, O mighty one,
whose eyes are charming like lotus blossoms, captivating with the sound of the Sāmas,
whose self is the parting ornament of the Vedic texts, the soul of all, of beautiful strides,
praised by the four-faced Brahmā and Śaṃbhu, O wide-eyed one!

Now, the arrival of the lord Varāha along with Earth at Śeṣācala:
Mounting Garuda, the lord of birds, he went to Vṛṣabhācala,
the lord of the earth being praised by the lords of sages headed by Nārada.
On the western bank of the Svāmipuṣkariṇī, revered by the world,
the boar-faced one sits, worshipped there by lords of sages,
by the highly fortunate Vaikhānasa sages, equal to Brahmā, great souls.

Now, the fruit of hearing this chapter:
"Whoever reads this purifying, righteous dialogue of us two, O Sūta,
either before the deity or before brahmins,
while people of all social classes listen with devotion,
he attains high standing, accompanied by sons and grandsons.
And whatever is desired by all those who listen, that shall come to pass."
Sūta said:
"Thus the venerable Vyāsa, attended by sages, spoke to me.
Just as it was heard by me formerly from the teacher Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana,
precisely that has all been related here by me, O lords of sages."
Having heard Sūta's words in this way, they became delighted in mind.
The seers said:
"O Sūta, you have told us the māhātmya of the holy mountain among holy mountains on earth,
named Ahīndra, which removes sins and grants the fruit of liberation.

2.1.d: शृणु देवि परं गुह्यं सद्यः संपत्तिकारकम् ..
2.1.m: 'Listen, O goddess, to the supreme secret, which instantly brings prosperity,
which grants land, grants sons, is to be kept secret, and never to be disclosed [indiscriminately].

2.1.s: kiṃ ca śuśrūṣave vācyaṃ bhaktāya niyatātmane .. 9 ..
2.1.d: किं च शुश्रूषवे वाच्यं भक्ताय नियतात्मने .. 9 ..
2.1.m: Yet it should be spoken to one who desires to hear, who is devoted and self-controlled:
"Om, salutations to the glorious Varāha and the lifter of the Earth,"
joined with the wife of Fire (svāhā), should ever be recited by those seeking liberation.
This mantra, O goddess Earth, grants all perfections.

2.1.s: ṛṣiḥ saṃkarṣaṇaḥ prokto devatā tvahameva hi .. 11 ..
2.1.d: ऋषिः संकर्षणः प्रोक्तो देवता त्वहमेव हि .. 11 ..
2.1.m: Its seer is declared to be Saṃkarṣaṇa, and I myself am the deity;
the meter is proclaimed to be paṅkti, and 'Śrī' is stated to be the seed-syllable.
Having received that mantra from a true guru, one should chant the mantra four hundred thousand times,
and make offerings of milk-rice mixed with honey and clarified butter.
Now I shall describe the visualization that brings purity of mind:
Splendid like a mountain of pure crystal, with eyes like red lotus petals,
having the face of a boar, gentle, four-armed, wearing a diadem,
with the śrīvatsa on his chest, holding a discus, conch, and lotus, with a hand granting fearlessness,
accompanied by you, O ocean-clad one, seated on my left thigh,
wearing red and yellow garments, adorned with red ornaments,
seated upon a lotus upon the form of Śeṣa stationed in the middle of the back of the divine Turtle.

2.1.s: evaṃ dhyātvā japenmaṃtraṃ sadā cāṣṭottaraṃ śatam ..
2.1.d: एवं ध्यात्वा जपेन्मंत्रं सदा चाष्टोत्तरं शतम् ..
2.1.m: Having thus meditated, one should constantly chant the mantra one hundred and eight times;
he attains all desires, and at the end surely goes to liberation.

2.1.s: proktaṃ mayā te dharaṇi yatpṛṣṭo'haṃ tvayā'male ..
2.1.d: प्रोक्तं मया ते धरणि यत्पृष्टोऽहं त्वयाऽमले ..
2.1.m: O Earth, O pure one, what you asked me has been declared by me.

2.1.s: ataḥ kiṃ te vyavasitaṃ brūhi tadvimalānane .. 18 ..
2.1.d: अतः किं ते व्यवसितं ब्रूहि तद्विमलानने .. 18 ..
2.1.m: Therefore, what is your intention? Speak it, O fair-faced one.
Now begins the description of the attainment of the desired objects of Dharma and others through the mantra of Śrī Varāha.
Śrī Sūta said:

2.1.s: etacchrutvā tato bhūmiḥ papraccha punareva tam ..
2.1.d: एतच्छ्रुत्वा ततो भूमिः पप्रच्छ पुनरेव तम् ..
2.1.m: Having heard this, the Earth then questioned him once again:

2.1.s: kenaivānuṣṭhitaṃ deva purā prāptaṃ phalaṃ ca kim .. 19 ..

2.1.m: "By whom was this performed in ancient times, O Lord, and what fruit was obtained?"
Thus asked, the divine Śrī Varāha spoke this again:

2.1.s: purā kṛtayuge devi dharmo nāma manurmahān .. 2.1.2.20 ..
2.1.d: पुरा कृतयुगे देवि धर्मो नाम मनुर्महान् .. 2.1.2.20 ..
2.1.m: "Long ago, in the Kṛta age, O goddess, there was a great Manu named Dharma.
Having received this mantra from Brahmā and chanting it on this mountain,

2.1.s: māṃ ca dṛṣṭvā varaṃ labdhvā prāpto'bhūnmāmakaṃ padam .. 21 ..
2.1.d: मां च दृष्ट्वा वरं लब्ध्वा प्राप्तोऽभून्मामकं पदम् .. 21 ..
2.1.m: and seeing me and receiving a boon, he attained my own abode.
Long ago, Indra, fallen from heaven on account of Durvāsas's curse,
having worshipped me here with this [mantra], O goddess, reached heaven again.

2.1.s: anye'pi munayo bhūme japtvā prāptāḥ parāṃ gatim ..
2.1.d: अन्येऽपि मुनयो भूमे जप्त्वा प्राप्ताः परां गतिम् ..
2.1.m: Other sages too, O Earth, having chanted it, attained the highest state.
Indeed, Ananta, the lord of serpents, having received this from Kaśyapa,
chanted it in Śvetadvīpa and became the bearer of the earth.
Therefore, it should always be chanted here by men desirous of the earth."
Śrī Sūta said:
Having heard this, well pleased, she spoke once more to the Bearer of the Earth:
Dhāraṇī said:
"On the great mountain named Veṅkaṭa, when will Śrīnivāsa, the lord of the world,
the flawless lord of gods, come together with Śrī and Bhūmi?
How will Janārdana remain there until the end of the kalpa?
Tell this, O essence of the Boar! Great is my curiosity."

2.1.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīveṃkaṭācalamāhātmye dharaṇīvarāhasaṃvāde śrīvarāhamaṃtrārādhanavidhyādivarṇanaṃnāma dvitīyo'dhyāyaḥ .. 2 ..
2.1.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीवेंकटाचलमाहात्म्ये धरणीवराहसंवादे श्रीवराहमंत्राराधनविध्यादिवर्णनंनाम द्वितीयोऽध्यायः .. 2 ..
2.1.m: Thus ends the second chapter, named 'Description of the Rule for Worshipping with the Śrī Varāha Mantra and Others' in the dialogue between Dharaṇī and Varāha, in the Śrīveṅkaṭācalamāhātmya of the second, Vaiṣṇava section of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Now begins the description of the Lord becoming visible to all people at the prayer of Agastya.
Śrī Varāha said:
"Well, I shall tell you what happened in the past, O fair-faced one.
Listen, O great goddess, to the holy [account], including what will be and what follows.
In the Vaivasvata interval, O goddess, during the former Kṛta age,
having seen the great austerity of Vāyu, O sinless one, accompanied by Śrī and Bhūmi,
Śrīnivāsa came to the bank of the Svāmipuṣkariṇī.
In this most sacred aerial chariot named Ānanda, on the southern side,

2.1.s: vasiṣyati ca śrīkāṃto vāyoḥ priyakaro hariḥ .. 3 ..
2.1.d: वसिष्यति च श्रीकांतो वायोः प्रियकरो हरिः .. 3 ..
2.1.m: Hari, the beloved of Śrī, doing what pleases Vāyu, will dwell.
From then on, worshipped unceasingly by the commander of the army, Hṛṣīkeśa
will dwell in this aerial chariot invisible until the end of the kalpa."
Dhāraṇī said:
"Being invisible, how will the Blessed One become visible to mortals?
And Śrīnivāsa, the lord of gods, situated on your right side—
tell this, O lord of the suras: how will he be worshipped by people?"
Śrī Varāha said:
"Agastya, having arrived here and seen the eternal God,
having worshipped him for twelve years and gratified him again and again,
begged for his presence there, saying: 'May you become visible!'
Thus addressed, Hṛṣīkeśa, accompanied by Śrī and Bhūmi, O Earth,
the Blessed Lord spoke:
'For your sake, I shall become visible to all embodied beings.
This aerial chariot, O celestial seer, will never be visible;
until the end of the kalpa, O chief of sages, I shall be visible in this; of this there is no doubt.'
Having heard his words, the sage, delighted, went to his own hermitage.
Then that four-armed God became visible to human beings and others,
seated in this aerial chariot conceived by sages, facing the north. // 11
Being worshipped by Skanda, constantly attended by Vāyu,
in this way a great age consisting of four yugas passed away. // 12
Now begins the description of the birth of the son named Ākāśarāja to Mitravarmā.
O Earth, when the twenty-eighth [Dvāpara] occurred, at the end of the Dvāpara [yuga],

2.1.s: yuddhe ca bhārate'tīte tiṣye sati yuge tathā .. 13 ..
2.1.d: युद्धे च भारतेऽतीते तिष्ये सति युगे तथा .. 13 ..
2.1.m: when the Bhārata war had passed, and when the Kali yuga had likewise arrived, // 13
kings such as Vikramārka, Śakas, Śūdras, and others,
will go to heaven without knowing Me, O fair-faced one. // 14
Then Mitravarmā, born in the Lunar dynasty, a great car-warrior,
a king in the Tuṇḍīra realm residing in Nārāyaṇapura, // 15
great and blessed with great fortune, will arise, O woman of shapely hips.
While that lord of the earth governs the world of mortals with righteousness, // 16
the earth, bearing crops without ploughing, adorned with all grains,
and all the people became free from plagues and devoted to righteousness. // 17
His wife was a charming Pāṇḍya princess.

2.1.s: tasya jajñe kulottaṃso viyannāmā suto'sya vai .. 18 ..
2.1.d: तस्य जज्ञे कुलोत्तंसो वियन्नामा सुतोऽस्य वै .. 18 ..
2.1.m: To him was born a son, the crest-jewel of his family, indeed named Viyat. // 18
His wife was named Dharaṇī, born of the Śaka race.
Having entrusted the kingdom to him, Mitravarmā, the best of kings, // 19
went to the holy penance-grove near Mount Veṅkaṭa. // 2.1.3.20
Now begins the account of the emergence of Padmāvatī from the surface of the earth.
The one named Ākāśa became a great universal monarch.
A king committed to the vow of monogamy, his heart was devoted to Dharaṇī. // 21
For a sacrifice, he cleared the ground on the bank of the Araṇī.
While the surface of the earth was being ploughed with a golden plough, // 22
as he scattered a handful of seeds, a maiden was seen arisen from the ground,
lying on a bed of lotuses, lovely, endowed with all auspicious marks, // 23
shining like a doll made of refined gold.
Seeing her, the king, his eyes wide with astonishment, // 24
taking [her, thought,] “This is indeed my daughter!” again and again.
He rejoiced with his ministers, and an incorporeal voice said to him: // 25
“Truly she is your own daughter; raise this fair-eyed one.”

2.1.s: tataḥ prītamanā rājā svapuraṃ praviveśa ha .. 26 ..
2.1.d: ततः प्रीतमना राजा स्वपुरं प्रविवेश ह .. 26 ..
2.1.m: Then, delighted in mind, the king entered his own city. // 26
Summoning Queen Dharaṇī, the ruler of the earth said this:
“Behold this [child], given by the gods to me, risen from the surface of the earth. // 27
She will surely be the daughter for both of us who are childless.”

2.1.s: ityuktvā pradadau devyā haste prītyā viyannṛpaḥ .. 28 ..
2.1.d: इत्युक्त्वा प्रददौ देव्या हस्ते प्रीत्या वियन्नृपः .. 28 ..
2.1.m: Having spoken thus, King Viyat gladly placed [her] in the hand of the queen. // 28
Now begins the birth of the son named Vasudāna to Ākāśarāja through his wife named Dharaṇī.
When she entered the house, Dharaṇī conceived a pregnancy.
And King Viyat, delighted upon seeing her with affectionate eyes, // 29

2.1.d: उवाच फलिता सुभ्रुर्लता सान्तानिकी च मे .. 2.1.3.30 ..
2.1.m: said, “O woman of lovely eyebrows, my wish-fulfilling creeper of offspring has borne fruit.” // 2.1.3.30

2.1.m: Then Queen Dharaṇī, lotus-eyed,
at the proper time, at a highly auspicious hour, when five planets were in their exaltation, // 31

2.1.s: graheṣu suṣuve putraṃ meṣasthe ca divākare .. 31 ..
2.1.d: ग्रहेषु सुषुवे पुत्रं मेषस्थे च दिवाकरे .. 31 ..
2.1.m: and when the sun was in Aries, gave birth to a son.
Divine kettle-drums sounded; a rain of flowers fell upon the house;
a wind pleasant to the touch blew then on the day of his birth. // 32
Highly delighted at the birth of a son, to those who announced the birth of the son,
he made a gift of all his possessions, with the exception of the royal parasol and fly-whisks. // 33
He also made a gift of ten million tawny cows and more than a hundred bulls.
On the twelfth auspicious day, he performed the birth-rites and other ceremonies,

2.1.s: cakāra nāmadheyaṃ ca vasudāna iti svayam .. 34 ..
2.1.d: चकार नामधेयं च वसुदान इति स्वयम् .. 34 ..
2.1.m: and himself gave [him] the name Vasudāna. // 34
The glorious Varāha said:
O goddess, Vasudāna, the delightful son of Ākāśa,
grew day by day, like the moon, the king of stars, in the bright fortnight. // 35
Invested with the sacred thread, he was disciplined by preceptors who had mastered the Veda;
he also learned from his father missiles and weapons along with their mantras. // 36
He studied the four-limbed science of archery along with its auxiliary branches.
Through him, who was exceedingly mighty, the father became invincible to enemies, // 37

2.1.d: आकाश इव निष्पंको ग्रीष्मे भानुमता युतः ..
2.1.m: like the clear sky joined with the radiant sun in summer,
like [the sun] at midday in Vaiśākha, unbearable and difficult to gaze upon. // 38

Śrī Varāha said:
Those maidens answered him: "None has been seen by us. // 40
Why have you, a bearer of an excellent bow, come to our forest?
All the beasts living here are unslayable, O king of hunters!" // 41
"Depart quickly from this forest protected by King Ākāśa."
Hearing their words, he dismounted from his horse.
"Who are you, and who is this maiden resembling a lotus,
charming, lovely in all her limbs, with full and high breasts?
Tell me; having heard, I shall go to the mountain, my abode."
Hearing his words, prompted by the daughter of Dharanī,
the friend Padmāvatī spoke to the hunter whose dwelling is the mountain:
"She is the daughter of King Ākāśa, born from the surface of the earth,
our mistress, O hero, known by name as Padminī.
Tell us, O handsome-formed one: what is your name, or whose son are you?
What is your caste, where is your dwelling, and for what purpose have you come here?"
Thus questioned, he spoke to them with a gentle smile upon his lotus-face:

2.1.m:
Thus rebuked by them, mounting his swift-going horse,
joined by all his followers, he went very swiftly to the mountain.
Thus ends the fourth chapter, entitled 'Narration of the Arrival of Nārada near Padmāvatī Dwelling in the Garden, the Hunt of Śrīnivāsa, and Other Events', in the dialogue between Dharanī and Varāha in the Māhātmya of Mount Śrīveṅkaṭa, in the second Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, of the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

2.1.m:
Now follows the arrival of Nārada near Padmāvatī who dwells in the garden:
The Earth said: / The name of the son of Ākāśarāja was spoken by the Lord. / What name did he then give to his daughter who was not born from a womb? // 1
Śrī Sūta said: / Thus asked, Śrī Varāha, the Lord of the universe, spoke again: // 2
Śrī Varāha said: / Wise King Ākāśarāja, seeing her lying on a lotus, // 3
gave that daughter of the earth the name Padminī. / Now, when she had attained youth and was surrounded by her female friends, // 4
sporting in a pleasure-grove echoing with parrots and cuckoos, / Nārada, the best of sages, arrived there by chance. // 5
Beholding her like the goddess of the forest, he spoke thus in wonder: // 6
Nārada said: / "Who are you, timid maiden? Whose daughter are you? Show me your hand." / Addressed thus, she of most charming limbs revealed herself to the sage: // 7
"O brahmin, I am the daughter of King Ākāśarāja; tell me my auspicious marks." / Spoken to in this way, Nārada, the best of sages, then replied: // 8
Now the marks of Padmāvatī's body as described by Nārada:
Nārada said: / "Listen, fair-faced one! I shall declare your bodily marks to you. / O lady with lovely eyebrows, your feet are firm, endowed with petals of red lotuses. // 9
Your toes are even, red, and endowed with red, elevated nails. / Your ankles are concealed and symmetrical; your shanks are hairless and auspicious. // 10
Your knees are even and very smooth; your thighs are even and gradually broad. / Your buttocks are wide and plump; your hips are indeed worthy of meditation! // 11
Your navel is circular and deep; both your flanks are plump. / Your waist is delicate with three folds and adorned with a line of hair. // 12
Your breasts are plump, firm, smooth, elevated, and have recessed nipples. / Your hands resemble red lotuses, endowed with lotus lines,
extremely delicate, with reddish joints and unbroken, even fingers, // 13
adorned with a row of nails having the form of a parrot's beak.

2.1.m:
Long and tender, O auspicious lady, are your arms like stems of flowers. // 14
Your back shines like an altar, slender and straight in the middle. / Your neck is red and long, and your shoulders are sloping, O auspicious one! // 15
Your face is ever cheerful, with the luster of the spotless moon. / Your cheeks resemble mirrors of gold, radiant with earrings. // 16
Your nose has the form of a sesamum blossom, O fair-faced maiden! / Extremely enchanting, resembling the spotless eighth-day moon, // 17
this forehead of yours is seen, richly adorned with dark locks of hair. / Your head is evenly rounded and endowed with glossy, long hair. // 18
Your mouth possesses teeth that shine with a smile and is endowed with bimba-like lips. / Your face is worthy of Viṣṇu: this is my settled judgment. // 19
Your navel turns clockwise like a whirlpool born in the Gaṅgā. / Indeed, you appear just like Lakṣmī arisen from the ocean of milk!" // 20
Śrī Varāha said: / Having spoken thus, worshipped by them, Nārada then disappeared. / Hearing this, her female companions said to their friend Padminī: // 21
Now Padmāvatī's departure to the flower-forest with her companions:
"Let us go to the forest for flowers; springtime has arrived! / Karṇikāras, mangos, campakas, and coral trees; // 22
palāśas, pāṭalas, kundas, and red aśokas have blossomed! / Lotuses, sindhuvāras, mālatīs, and yūthikā creepers, // 23
kahlāras and karavīras have blossomed as if in mutual rivalry! / Let us gather flowers in this delightful forest!" // 24
Having said this, they went to the forest together with the daughter of Ākāśarāja. / Gathering flowers and wandering here and there, // 25
they saw a king of elephants shining with two white tusks, / lustrous with two streams of rut emerging from the slope of his temples, // 26
lofty, accompanied by herds of female elephants, shining with dust, / his face covered with fine spray issuing from his blowing trunk. // 27
Seeing him, with agitated hearts, they took refuge near a large tree.

Now the infatuation of Śrīnivāsa upon seeing Padmāvatī.
The glorious Varāha said:
Reaching his divine abode, dismounting from his excellent horse,
and dismissing all the gods in the form of hunters together with their followers,
saying, 'Take rest,' he entered the jeweled pavilion.
Ascending the jeweled staircase and crossing five chambers,
reaching the mansion of pearls, upon an auspicious, gently swinging
couch made of the nine gems, Hari lay down, helpless,
remembering that very wide-eyed maiden whose radiance was like the womb of a lotus,
slender-waisted, with full breasts and a face like a pleasing lotus with a gentle smile.
He deemed that auspicious lotus-born maiden to be none other than the daughter of the Ocean of Milk.

reaching the bank of the Araṇī and resting within the forest,
having beheld Nārāyaṇapurī, you will be filled with wonder.

densely crowded with groves of areca palms, orange trees, likuca, and coconut palms;
accompanied by jasmine, mālatī, kunda, yūthikā, and screw-pine;

The Gandharva chiefs sang, and hosts of apsarases danced;
Celestial kettledrums sounded then in the Lord's presence;

The Lord, accompanied by the host of gods and attendants such as Viṣvaksena,

2.1.m: “I will tell you, O Goddess; listen to what will happen in the future as I describe it to you.
On this holy mountain there was a Niṣāda named Vasu.
He was a guard of the śyāmāka field, devoted to Puruṣottama.
Cooking the grains of śyāmāka and sprinkling them with honey,
he offered them to the God of gods who is accompanied by Śrī and Bhūmi.
To him who was thus devoted, his auspicious young wife, Citravatī,
bore an excellent son named Vīra.
Vasu, together with his son and his wife devoted to her husband,
on a certain day said to his son, ‘Guard the śyāmāka,’
and having left him behind, set out with his wife, intent on searching for honey.
He quickly went to another forest, wishing to see a honeycomb.
The boy, taking the cooked grains of śyāmāka and putting them in the fire,
Having crushed [them], he offered [them] at the root of the tree to the Lord of Śrī.
Having eaten the food-offering, the brave boy sat at ease.
Meanwhile, Vasu also arrived, bringing the honey.
Seeing the grains eaten, he scolded his son,
and, taking a sword to kill him, hastily raised his hand.
Now the Lord's speech to Vasu, who was bent on killing his son:
Then Viṣṇu, abiding in that tree, seized the sword with his hand.

Now the construction of the divine garden, pavilion, and other works by Raṅgadāsa for Śrīnivāsa:
Having thus seen Śrīnivāsa, Raṅgadāsa was filled with wonder,
and thought: “I will make a garden for this god.”
Having resolved everything in his mind, the wise man lived at the foot of a tree,
providing day by day through the Vaikhānasa a food-offering for Viṣṇu.
Gradually clearing the thick forest, he cut down the adjacent trees,
[sparing only] the tamarind tree of the god's assembly and the campaka tree of Ramā;
commanded by the god, he left aside both of them, which were served by the god.
Then, all around the god, he built a stone wall upon the ground.
All around that very wall, he planted flower gardens:
jasmine, oleander, lotus, kunda, mandāra, and mālatī;
and he planted whole groves of tulasī and campaka.
Digging a well there, he nourished the grove with its water.

He was born into the exalted Lunar dynasty, renowned as Toṇḍamān,

From the age of five, devotion to Viṣṇu arose in that naturally wise prince,
a great mine of virtues such as good character, valor, and strength.
He married Padmā, the enchanting daughter of the Pāṇḍya king.

Now, the account of the five-colored parrot near Śrīnivāsa:
Seeing a five-colored parrot, he pursued it wishing to seize it.
Uttering "Śrīnivāsa!", it flew swiftly toward the mountain.
Pursuing it, the king also ascended the king of mountains,
observing various caves and peaks all around.
Searching for the parrot, he entered a forest of wild rice.
Not seeing that excellent parrot, he beheld a forest guardian.
Seeing the king approaching, he quickly went out to meet him.
having bowed down full of humility, he stood with folded hands.
Toṇḍamān too honoured him and asked that forester:
"Was a five-coloured parrot seen by you coming here?
Saying 'Śrīnivāsa', where has it gone, O forester?"
The forester said:
"That five-coloured [parrot], O lord of kings, is ever dear to Śrīnivāsa.
Always staying by his side, he was reared by Śrī and Bhūmi.
On the bank of Svāmipuṣkariṇī he ever stays in the god's presence.

Now the praise of Śrī Lakṣmī made by the gods and others.
The gods said:
Obeisance to Śrī, the bearer of the worlds, the mother of Brahmā; obeisance, obeisance!
Obeisance to you who have lotus eyes, whose face is a lotus; obeisance, obeisance!
To the one whose lotus face is serene, who has the radiance of a lotus; obeisance, obeisance!
Obeisance to the one who dwells in the bilva forest, the wife of Viṣṇu; obeisance, obeisance!
To the one wearing exquisite silk, who has broad hips; obeisance, obeisance!
To the one whose breasts are plump and high like ripe bilva fruit; obeisance, obeisance!
O auspicious one, whose palms and soles resemble the petals of a deep-red lotus,
Adorned with armlets of fine gems, bracelets, a girdle, and anklets,
Whose whole body is anointed with yakṣakardama paste, radiant with bangles,
Decorated with various auspicious ornaments and pearl necklaces,
Whose lotus face shines with earrings and ear ornaments,
With a lotus in your hand, obeisance to you; be pleased, O beloved of Hari!
To you, who are knowledge embodied as the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman; obeisance, obeisance!
Be pleased; look upon us with casts of your merciful glance, O daughter of the ocean!
Those who are seen by you attain the status of Brahmā, Rudra, or Indra.

2.1.m: Going to Kurvapura, he went to the house of that potter.
Seeing the king arrive, [the potter] bowed down and stood before him.
To that standing man named Bhīma, the best of kings inquired:
Toṇḍamān said:

2.1.s: bhīma pūjayase devaṃ kathaṃ vada kulottama .. 2.1.10.90 ..

2.1.m: "Bhīma, tell me: how do you worship the god, O best of your lineage?"
The venerable Varāha said:

2.1.s: pṛṣṭaḥ prāha kulālo'pi jātu jāne na cārcanam ..

Bhīma said:

[namely] Toṇḍamān, and there is a conversation with him, then you shall attain liberation."
Such was the boon that the god Veṅkaṭeśvara granted previously.
Now the attainment of Vaikuṇṭha by the devotee named Bhīma of Kurva village together with his wife:

2.1.m: Having spoken thus, the potter, together with his wife,
seeing an aerial chariot arrived and seeing the god Janārdana,
bowing down, gave up his life-breaths, that best of devotees with his wife.
And while the king of kings watched, mounting the aerial chariot,

2.1.m: Seeing this wonder there and having reached his own city, the king was delighted.
Having anointed according to rule his own son named Śrīnivāsa, [he said:]
"Protect the people and the earth according to righteousness."
Having thus instructed his son, the wise one performed supreme austerity.
As he was performing austerity, the god Hari appeared before his eyes.
Now King Toṇḍamān's attainment of similar form [to the Lord] through the grace of Śrīnivāsa:
Mounting Garuḍa, the god [appeared], accompanied by Ramā and Bhūmi.
The Lord said:
"What can I do [for you], O best of kings? I am pleased with your austerity."
Thus addressed by the god of gods, Toṇḍamān, the king of kings,
became overjoyed, joined his palms, and spoke with a choked voice:
"I desire to dwell in your realm, which is free from old age and death.
Grant me this very boon, O Mādhava; this is what I desire."
The venerable Varāha said:
Having spoken thus, he fell to the earth with eight limbs in prostration before the god.

2.1.s: tadā kalevaraṃ muktvā vimānaṃ tvāruroha ca .. .. 104 ..

2.1.m: Then, abandoning his mortal body, he mounted the aerial chariot.
Praised by the Gandharvas, having attained a form like that of the bow-wielder,
where grief and delusion are destroyed, free from old age and death,
from which there is no return, he attained that abode of Viṣṇu.
Now the declaration of the fruits of hearing and reciting this māhātmya:
"This future event has been related by me, O goddess, O lady of fair complexion.
Whoever causes it to be heard, or whoever hears it, goes to the realm of Viṣṇu."
The venerable Sūta said:
Thus what was spoken by the god of gods, together with what is future and what follows,
whoever hears or recites with devotion this auspicious ancient narrative,
having enjoyed all desires, goes in the end to the abode of Viṣṇu.

2.1.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīveṃkaṭācalamāhātmye dharaṇīvarāhasaṃvāde bhaviṣyadvarṇane toṇḍamāṃścakravartivṛttavarṇanaṃnāma daśamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 10 ..

The venerable Sūta said:
Now the destruction of the great sin of Kāśyapa through bathing in Svāmipuṣkariṇī:
Now, therefore, having taken as my subject an auspicious sacred narrative
concerning the auspicious Svāmipuṣkariṇī, I shall relate it, O best of the twice-born.
Formerly, a twice-born named Kāśyapa, in this auspicious, best of sacred fords,
having bathed, was freed from a very great sin that leads to hell.
The seers said:
"O sage, what sin did this one named Kāśyapa commit,
from which he was freed in an instant by bathing here in the best of sacred fords?
Tell this to us who are full of faith, O Sūta, through the power of your compassion;
for us who are sated with the nectar of your speech, there is no thirst at all."
The venerable Sūta said:
"Expounding the māhātmya of the venerable Svāmipuṣkariṇī,
I shall tell an ancient narrative that destroys the sin of those who recite it.
Now the narrative of Parīkṣit:
There was a king, the son of Abhimanyu, Parīkṣit by name.
resided in Hāstinapura, protecting the earth according to dharma.

2.1.s: sa rājā jātu vipine cacāra mṛgayārataḥ ..
2.1.d: स राजा जातु विपिने चचार मृगयारतः ..
2.1.m: Once that king wandered in the forest, devoted to the hunt.
The king, sixty years of age, was afflicted with hunger and thirst.
Eagerly tracking a deer that had vanished in the forest,
the best of monarchs saw a sage engrossed in meditation and said:

2.1.s: mayā bāṇena vipine mṛgo viddho'dhunā mune ..
2.1.d: मया बाणेन विपिने मृगो विद्धोऽधुना मुने ..
2.1.m: “O sage, a deer was just now struck by my arrow in the forest.

2.1.m: Was it seen by you, O wise one, as it fled, trembling with fear?”
Fixed in samādhi, because of his silence, he said nothing at all.

2.1.m: Then, with the notch of his bow, upon the shoulder of that great sage,

2.1.m: Do not be arrogant, my friend, and do not be angry at this in vain.”

2.1.m: Śṛṅgin became furious, eager to utter a curse upon the king:
“Whoever placed a dead snake upon my father, foolish in mind—
let him die within seven nights, bitten by the serpent Takṣaka!”
Thus the sage's son cursed Parīkṣit, the son of Subhadrā's son.

2.1.s: śamīkākhyaḥ pitā tasya śaptaṃ śrutvā sutena tam ..

2.1.m: His father, named Śamīka, hearing that the king had been cursed by his son,
the eminent sage spoke to his son Śṛṅgin:
“Why have you cursed the king, the protector of all the worlds?
In a kingless world, how shall we safely dwell?
From anger sin arises; through compassion happiness is attained.
He who dispels aroused anger through patience alone,
enjoys supreme happiness in this world and in the next.

2.1.s: kṣamāyuktā hi puruṣā labhaṃte śreya uttamam .. 19 ..
2.1.d: क्षमायुक्ता हि पुरुषा लभंते श्रेय उत्तमम् .. 19 ..
2.1.m: For persons endowed with patience attain the highest good.”

2.1.m: Then Śamīka spoke to his own disciple named Gauramukha:

2.1.d: भो गौरमुख गत्वा त्वं वद भूपं परीक्षितम् .. 2.1.11.20 ..

Thus addressed by Śamīka, Gauramukha went to the king.
Having approached King Parīkṣit, the son of Subhadrā's son, he said:

2.1.s: dṛṣṭvā sarpaṃ pituḥ skaṃdhe tvayā vinihitaṃ mṛtam ..

2.1.m: “Seeing a dead snake placed by you upon his father's shoulder,

2.1.s: śamīkasya sutaḥ śṛṅgī śaśāpa tvāṃ ruṣānvitaḥ .. 23 ..
2.1.d: शमीकस्य सुतः शृङ्गी शशाप त्वां रुषान्वितः .. 23 ..
2.1.m: Śamīka's son Śṛṅgin, filled with fury, cursed you:
‘On the seventh day from this day, by the great serpent Takṣaka
may the son of Abhimanyu be quickly bitten and burned by poison-fire!’

2.1.s: evaṃ śaśāpa tvāṃ rājañchṛṃgī tasya muneḥ sutaḥ ..
2.1.d: एवं शशाप त्वां राजञ्छृंगी तस्य मुनेः सुतः ..
2.1.m: Thus Śṛṅgin, the son of that sage, cursed you, O king.
His father sent me to your presence to tell you this.”
Having said this to the king, Gauramukha quickly departed.
After Gauramukha had left, the king was overwhelmed with sorrow.
Then, sky-scraping, lofty, supported by a single pillar, very extensive—
a pavilion in the midst of the Gaṅgā the eminent king erected.
With physicians skilled in the great Gāruḍa mantras and skilled in medicinal herbs,
he made concentrated effort to counteract Takṣaka's poison.
Surrounded by many foremost gods, divine seers, and royal seers,
the king, devoted to Viṣṇu, sat in that lofty pavilion.
At that juncture, a brahmin, Kāśyapa, the foremost of mantra-experts,
set out to protect the king from the potent poison of Takṣaka.
On the seventh day, the eminent twice-born, poor and desirous of wealth, [went].
Meanwhile, Takṣaka also arrived, disguised as a brahmin.
Seeing Kāśyapa on the way, he spoke to him:

2.1.s: brāhmaṇa tvaṃ kutra yāsi vada me'dya mahāmune .. 32 ..
2.1.d: ब्राह्मण त्वं कुत्र यासि वद मेऽद्य महामुने .. 32 ..
2.1.m: “O brahmin, where are you going? Tell me today, O great sage!”
Thus questioned, the twice-born Kāśyapa then said to Takṣaka:
“Today Takṣaka with his poison-fire will burn the great king
Parīkṣit; to quell that, I am approaching his presence.”

2.1.s: ityuktaḥ sa ca taṃ vipraṃ takṣakaḥ punarabravīt .. 34 ..

even in a hundred years, nor even by tens of thousands of great mantras.
If you now have the power to treat someone bitten by me,
I will bite a tree that is many yojanas high; revive it!

2.1.s: tato bhavānsamartho hītyevaṃ me bhāti he dvija ..
2.1.d: ततो भवान्समर्थो हीत्येवं मे भाति हे द्विज ..
2.1.m: Then, O twice-born, it will appear to me that you are indeed capable."
Having spoken thus, Takṣaka then bit that tree;
and that exceedingly tall tree was reduced to ashes.
Earlier, a man had climbed that very tree;
he too was then burned by the fiery blasts of Takṣaka's poison.

2.1.s: tannaraṃ na vijajñāte tau ca kāśyapatakṣakau .. 39 ..

"Let all, beginning with the brahmins, witness my mantra power now!"
Having spoken thus, Kāśyapa, the best of mantra-masters,
revived by the power of his mantras that tree reduced to ashes by the fire of poison.
That man was also brought back to life along with the tree.
Then Takṣaka said to that Kāśyapa, skilled in mantras:

2.1.s: yathā na munivāṅmithyā bhavedevaṃ kuru dvija ..
2.1.d: यथा न मुनिवाङ्मिथ्या भवेदेवं कुरु द्विज ..

2.1.m: Perceiving through his eye of wisdom that the king was short-lived, Kāśyapa

2.1.s: yūyaṃ taṃ nṛpatiṃ prāpya munīnāṃ veṣadhāriṇaḥ ..
2.1.d: यूयं तं नृपतिं प्राप्य मुनीनां वेषधारिणः ..
2.1.m: "Go to that king, disguised as sages,
and swiftly offer fruits as gifts to Parīkṣit."

Takṣaka too, having assumed the form of an insect
in a certain jujube fruit, waited there to bite the king.
Then King Parīkṣit, having distributed to his elder ministers
all the fruits offered by all those disguised as brahmins,
out of curiosity took one large fruit in his hand.
At that moment, the sun too dipped behind the Western Mountain.
"May the seer's word not prove false!"—thus the people there,
all the brahmins and kings, said to one another then.
While all were speaking thus, a very red insect

2.1.s: sādhu raktaḥ kṛmiḥ sarvai rājñā cāpi parīkṣitā .. 53 ..

"Could this worm bite me today?" said the king,

Then Takṣaka, who was in the fruit in the form of an insect,

Thereupon, O brahmins, by the extremely powerful poison-fire of Takṣaka,
the king, along with his palace, was swiftly burned to ashes.
Having performed the funeral rites for that king, the ministers along with the royal priests,
desiring the protection of the world, consecrated his son
named Janamejaya as king over the kingdom.
The brahmin and excellent sage named Kāśyapa, who had come to protect the king from Takṣaka,

2.1.s: yo brāhmaṇo muniśreṣṭhaḥ sa sarvairniṃdito janaiḥ .. 59 ..

He wandered through all countries, condemned by all righteous folk;

2.1.s: steyaṃ saṃsargadoṣo vā mayā nācaritaṃ kvacit ..

2.1.m: If you know, Śākalya, tell me the fault I have committed."

Now, deliverance from hells such as Tāmisra through ritual ablution in Svāmipuṣkariṇī.
The seers said:
O Sūta, knower of the truth of all matters, who have reached the far shore of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas,
tell us, O lord, the glory of the glorious Svāmipuṣkariṇī,
by merely remembering which a man on earth may become liberated.
The glorious Sūta said:

2.1.s: svāmitīrthaṃ praśaṃsanti snāṃti vā kathayaṃti ye ..
2.1.d: स्वामितीर्थं प्रशंसन्ति स्नांति वा कथयंति ये ..
2.1.m: Those who praise the Svāmitīrtha, bathe in it, or narrate [its glory],
do not experience the hells in their twenty-eight varieties:
Tāmisra, Andhatāmisra, Mahāraurava, Raurava,
Kumbhīpāka, Kālasūtra, and Asipatravana;
Kṛmibhakṣa, Andhakūpa, Saṃdaṃśa, and Śālmalī;
Lālābhakṣa, Avīci, and Sārameyādana;
likewise Vajrakaṇṭaka, falling into Kṣārakardama,
devouring by hordes of Rakṣases, being impaled on a pike;
that named Tirodhāna, O brahmins, and the one named Sūcīmukha;
the consumption of pus and blood, and torment by poison and fire.
This collection of hells, twenty-eight in number,
a man does not go to, O brahmins, on account of immersing himself in the Svāmitīrtha.
A man who plunders the wealth, children, or wives of others,
bound by the noose of Time by the terrifying messengers of Yama,
is cast down into the dreadful hell Tāmisra for many years.
If he bathes in the Svāmitīrtha, he is not cast into that [hell].
The lowest of men who hates mother, father, or brahmins,
in the Kālasūtra hell, ten thousand yojanas wide,
scorched by fire below, and by the sun's rays above,
upon a copper floor, O brahmins, is cast down, afflicted with hunger.
If he bathes in the puṣkariṇī, he is not cast into that [hell].
A man who strays into a bad path, transgressing the way of the Veda,
is cast into the dreadful Asipatravana by the servants of Yama.
If he bathes in the Svāmitīrtha, however, he is not cast into that [hell].
A man who eats cooked food such as soup with partiality in the row,

2.1.s: akṛtvā paṃcayajñānvā bhuṃkte mohena sa dvijāḥ .. 15 ..
2.1.d: अकृत्वा पंचयज्ञान्वा भुंक्ते मोहेन स द्विजाः .. 15 ..
2.1.m: or eats through delusion without performing the five sacrifices, O twice-born,
is cast by Yama's soldiers into the hell of worm-eating;
being eaten by hundreds of worms while eating hordes of worms,
and becoming a worm himself, he would remain until the exhaustion of his sins.
If he bathes in the Svāmitīrtha, he is indeed not cast into that [hell].
He who steals the wealth of brahmins out of affection or by force,
or the wealth of others, whether a king or his servant,
tormented with tongs in fire-pits made of iron,
is cast into the terrible hell Saṃdaṃśa by Yama's men.
If he bathes in the Svāmitīrtha, however, he is not cast into that [hell].
The lowest of men who approaches an inaccessible woman,
or a woman who approaches an inaccessible man, O twice-born,
both of them, [forced to] embrace a glowing woman made of iron / and a man made of iron,
standing as long as the moon and the sun endure,
are cast into the dreadful hell named Sūcī by the servants of Yama.
And if he bathes in the Svāmitīrtha, he is not cast into that [hell].
He who torments all living beings through various means and afflictions,
is cast down into the dreadful hell Śālmalī, full of many thorns.
If he bathes in the Svāmitīrtha, however, he is not cast into that [hell].

2.1.s: rājā vā rājabhṛtyo vā yaḥ pāṣaṇḍamanudrutaḥ ..
2.1.d: राजा वा राजभृत्यो वा यः पाषण्डमनुद्रुतः ..
2.1.m: A king or a king's servant who has run after heresy,
a breaker of the barriers of dharma, is cast into Vaitaraṇī.
If he bathes in the Svāmitīrtha, however, he is not cast into that [hell].
Or one corrupted by association with an outcaste woman, devoid of purity and proper conduct,
abandoning shame, abandoning the Veda, always delighting in the behavior of beasts—
he, in [a hell] filled with pus, feces, urine, blood, phlegm, bile, and the like,
is cast down by the servants of Yama into an exceedingly disgusting hell.
Yet if he bathes in Svāmitīrtha, he is not cast down into it.
A hunter who torments wild deer with dogs or with arrows,
pierced with volleys of arrows in the other world by the servants of Yama,
is cast down by the servants of Yama into the hell named Prāṇarodha.
Yet if he bathes in Svāmitīrtha, he is not cast down into it.
A hypocrite devoid of the performance of Vedic rites who slaughters animals in sacrifice,
O twice-born, in the other worlds, into the hell Vaiśasa,
being hacked to pieces by Yama's soldiers, is cast down by the servants of Yama.
Yet if he bathes in the holy pool, he is not cast down into it.

2.1.s: ātmabhāryāṃ savarṇāṃ yo retaḥ pāyayate yadi ..
2.1.d: आत्मभार्यां सवर्णां यो रेतः पाययते यदि ..
2.1.m: If a man makes his own wife of the same class drink semen,
in the other world he, drinking semen, is cast down into the pit of semen (Retaḥkuṇḍa).
Yet if he bathes in the holy pool, he is not cast down into it.
A robber taking to the road, an administrator of poison, an arsonist of villages,
and a thief of merchants' goods, O best among the twice-born, in the other world,
is cast down for a long time into the terrible hell named Vajradaṃṣṭra.
Yet if he bathes in Svāmitīrtha, he is not cast down into it.

2.1.s: vidyante yāni cānyāni narakāṇi paratra vai .. 36 ..

2.1.m: Whatever other hells indeed exist in the other world,
a mortal does not encounter them, by virtue of immersing in Svāmitīrtha.
From bathing once in the holy pool, one obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice (aśvamedha);
knowledge of the self becomes directly perceptible, as well as the fourfold liberation;

2.1.s: na pāpe ramate buddhirna bhaveduḥkhameva vā .. 38 ..
2.1.d: न पापे रमते बुद्धिर्न भवेदुःखमेव वा .. 38 ..
2.1.m: the intellect does not delight in sin, nor does sorrow at all arise.
Whatever fruit is obtained by men through the gift of the person weighed against gold (tulāpuruṣa),
that fruit is attained by people through immersing in Svāmitīrtha.
Whatever merit indeed accrues to men through the gift of a thousand cows,
that merit a mortal gains through immersing in Svāmitīrtha.
Whichever of duty, wealth, desire, and liberation a man desires,
that very one he attains instantly through immersing in Svāmitīrtha.
Whether endowed with major sins (mahāpātaka) or endowed with all manner of sins,
he instantly becomes purified, O brahmins, through immersing in Svāmitīrtha.
Wisdom, fortune, renown, prosperity, knowledge, righteousness, detachment,
and purity of mind accrue to men through resorting to Svāmitīrtha.
Even ten thousand killings of a brahmin, ten thousand drinkings of liquor,
ten thousand violations of the teacher's wife by sinful doers,
ten thousand thefts of gold, and crores of associations with those [sinners]—
swiftly vanish through immersing in Svāmitīrtha.
Those [sins] equal to killing a brahmin, those equal to drinking liquor,
and those that are equal to violating the teacher's wife, O believers,
those equal to the theft of gold, and those equal to associating with them—
all of them perish through immersing in Svāmitīrtha.
Now, the attainment of great hell by those who lack faith in the greatness of Svāmitīrtha:
No doubt should ever be entertained concerning these things that have been spoken;

2.1.s: jihvāgre paraśuṃ taptaṃ prakṣipaṃti ca kiṃkarāḥ .. 48 ..

Oh, what foolishness! Oh, what foolishness! Oh, what foolishness, O best among the twice-born!
While the sacred ford called Svāmitīrtha, destroyer of all sins,
bestower of non-dual knowledge upon men, granter of enjoyment and liberation,
ever bestowing desired wishes, and likewise destroyer of ignorance,

2.1.s: aho mohasya māhātmyaṃ mayā vaktuṃ na śakyate .. 52 ..

For one who has bathed in Svāmitīrtha, there is truly no fear of Death.

2.1.m: Those men who behold Svāmitīrtha, bathe in it,

2.1.s: stuvanti ca praśaṃsaṃti spṛśaṃti ca namanti ca ..
2.1.d: स्तुवन्ति च प्रशंसंति स्पृशंति च नमन्ति च ..

2.1.s: na pibanti hi te stanyaṃ mātṝṇāṃ dvijapuṃgavāḥ .. 54 ..
2.1.d: न पिबन्ति हि ते स्तन्यं मातॄणां द्विजपुंगवाः .. 54 ..

2.1.s: evaṃ vaḥ kathitaṃ viprāḥ svāmitīrthasya vaibhavam ..

2.1.m: Thus has the glory of Svāmitīrtha been related to you, O brahmins;

2.1.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीवेंकटाचलमाहात्म्ये श्री स्वामिपुष्करिणीतीर्थमहिमानुवर्णनं नाम द्वादशोऽध्यायः .. 12 ..

Now, the description of the deeds of Dharmagupta:
The glorious Sūta said:
I will tell once more of the majesty of the Svāmitīrtha,
to you with respect, O dwellers of Naimiṣāraṇya. (1)
There was a great king named Nanda, born of the lunar dynasty;
he ruled with righteousness this earth bounded by the oceans. (2)
He had a son known as Dharmagupta.
Nanda placed the yoke of kingdom-protection upon his son, (3)
and, with senses conquered and food restrained, he entered the penance-forest.
When his father went to the penance-forest, the king named Dharmagupta, (4)
knowing righteousness and intent upon wise conduct, protected the earth.
He sacrificed with various sacrifices to the gods led by Indra. (5)

2.1.s: brāhmaṇānāṃ dadau vittaṃ kṣetrāṇi ca bahūni saḥ ..
2.1.d: ब्राह्मणानां ददौ वित्तं क्षेत्राणि च बहूनि सः ..
2.1.m: He gave wealth and many fields to the brahmins.
All people were devoted to their own duty while that king was ruling. (6)
At no time were there afflictions arising from thieves or the like under him.
Once, this Dharmagupta, having mounted an excellent horse, (7)
entered the forest, O best of brahmins, curious and fond of hunting.
With quarters filled with tamāla, tāla, hintāla, and kurava trees, (8)
he roamed about in that forest terrifying with lions and tigers,
whose directions were reverberating with the humming of intoxicated swarms of bees, (9)
crowded with groves of red lotuses, kalhāra, white lotuses, and blue water-lilies,
at a pond full of water, adorned by ascetics. (10)
While king Dharmagupta was wandering in that forest,
the night fell, O brahmins, its quarters enveloped in darkness. (11)
The king also, endowed with modesty, having performed the evening worship,

2.1.s: jajāpa ca vane tatra gāyatrīṃ vedamātaram .. 12 ..
2.1.d: जजाप च वने तत्र गायत्रीं वेदमातरम् .. 12 ..
2.1.m: chanted the Gāyatrī, the mother of the Vedas, there in the forest. (12)
When he had taken shelter in a certain tree out of fear of lions, tigers, and others,
a bear, tormented by fear of a lion, approached that prince. (13)
A solitary forest-dwelling lion ran after that tree.
Pursued by the lion, the bear climbed up the tree. (14)

2.1.s: āruhya ṛkṣo vṛkṣaṃ taṃ dadarśa jagatīpatim ..
2.1.d: आरुह्य ऋक्षो वृक्षं तं ददर्श जगतीपतिम् ..
2.1.m: Having climbed the tree, the bear saw the lord of the earth,
the great-souled one stationed in the tree, possessing great strength and valor. (15)
Having seen the king, that bear living in the forest said:

2.1.s: mā bhītiṃ kuru rājeṃdra vatsyāvo rajanīmiha .. 16 ..
2.1.d: मा भीतिं कुरु राजेंद्र वत्स्यावो रजनीमिह .. 16 ..
2.1.m: “Do not fear, O best of kings! We two shall spend the night here. (16)
Endowed with great courage and a huge body, possessing massive fangs,

Now begins the story of the twice-born named Sumati.
The glorious Sūta said:

How did he become attached to a Kirātī woman, O Sūta, best of Purāṇa reciters?

The glorious Sūta said:
In the region called Mahārāṣṭra, there was a certain pious brahmin
named Yajñadeva, who had mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas.
He was compassionate, hospitable, and a worshipper of Śiva and Nārāyaṇa.
To that Yajñadeva was born a son named Sumati.
Abandoning his father and his devoted wife,
he went away to the country of Utkala, devoted to the company of rogues.
A certain Kirātī woman living in that country, charming to young men,
had long been taking all the wealth of youths by enticing them.
Sumati, the lowest of brahmins, went to her house,

Now the greatness of the Rāmakṛṣṇatīrtha.
The venerable Sūta said:
"On the exceedingly holy [mountain] named Veṅkaṭa, which destroys all sins,
listen with great attention to the māhātmya of the Kṛṣṇatīrtha,
where merely by immersion even an ungrateful person is liberated.
Those who, bewildered by delusion, disrespect fathers, mothers, and elders,
and whatever other evil-minded, ungrateful, shameless people there may be—
all of them are purified in this Kṛṣṇatīrtha merely by a bath.
Formerly, a sage named Kṛṣṇa, on the mountain named Veṅkaṭa,
dwelt performing austerity, focused in meditation on Viṣṇu.
There he fashioned an excellent sacred ford for ritual ablution.
Having bathed there once, a mortal is freed, even if he were ungrateful.
In this regard, I shall recount an ancient legend that destroys sins,
by the mere hearing of which a person may attain liberation.
Long ago there was an eminent brahmin, the great sage Rāmakṛṣṇa,
truthful, virtuous, eloquent, endowed with compassion for all beings,
impartial to enemy and friend, self-restrained, an ascetic with senses conquered,
well-versed in the supreme Brahman, taking refuge solely in the reality of Brahman.
That sage of such power performed very severe austerity.
Remaining everywhere on the surface of the earth with all limbs motionless,
he did not move from his place by even the distance of an atom.
As he stayed there practicing austerity for many hundreds of years,

The glorious Sūta said:
On the very sacred [mountain] named Venkaṭa, especially to those tormented by thirst,
one who does not give water will attain birth as an animal.
Therefore, on the king of mountains, Venkaṭa, according to one's capacity,

Now begins Hemāṅga's attainment of the state of a house lizard due to not giving water.
Long ago, in the Ikṣvāku dynasty, there was a king named Hemāṅga,
devoted to brahmins, steeped in Brahman, having conquered his enemies and subdued his senses.
As many as are the particles of dust on earth, as many as are the drops of water,
as many as are the stars in the sky, so many cows would he give away.
By whom, through the darbha grass of sacrifices performed, the earth was known as Barhiṣmatī;
Many brahmins were satisfied with gifts of cows, land, sesame, gold, and the like.

He argued with specious reasons: “Merit lies in giving what is hard to obtain.”
He honored brahmins who were mutilated, impoverished, and worn down by lack of livelihood;
He did not honor learned brahmins who knew Brahman and discoursed on Brahman.

Now begins the description of the sacred field of Mount Veṅkaṭa and others.
Glorious Sūta said:
"I shall declare once again the māhātmya of Mount Veṅkaṭa
unto you with care; listen with completely focused minds.
Whatever sacred fords there are upon the earth and within the cosmic egg,
all of them exist on the mountain named Veṅkaṭa.
The Supreme Person dwelling on that best of meritorious mountains,
the auspicious God holding the conch and discus, wearing yellow garments,
whose chest is adorned with the Kaustubha jewel, the granter of fearlessness to devotees,
the God of gods, large-eyed, knowable through the Vedas, eternal—
People living in the countries of Aṅga, Kosala, Karṇāṭa, Kāśī, and Gurjara,
and those born in all regions such as Cola, Kerala, and Pāṇḍya,
come each year with their families to serve [Him];
as do the gods, seers, siddhas, and yogins such as Sanaka.
Those who perform service during the month of Bhādrapada

Now, the description of the continuous residence of Brahmā and others on the holy Mount Veṅkaṭa.
The glorious Sūta said:
Now, therefore, I shall describe the majesty of Mount Veṅkaṭa
to you with attentiveness; listen, being well concentrated! // 1
Hundreds of thousands and millions of lakes as well as rivers,
and most meritorious oceans, and even forests and hermitages;
holy sacred fields such as Vedāraṇya and others;
and sages headed by Vasiṣṭha, siddhas, cāraṇas, and kiṃnaras;
the Blessed Lord Madhusūdana together with Lakṣmī and Dharaṇī;
the Four-Faced One [Brahmā] accompanied indeed by Sāvitrī and Sarasvatī;
the Lord of Gods, the Three-Eyed One, Destroyer of Tripura, together with Pārvatī;
and the gods led by Indra, preceded by Heramba and the Six-Faced One [Skanda];
the planets headed by Āditya, and likewise the eight Vasus, O twice-born ones;
the ancestors, the guardians of the worlds, and other hosts of deities—
in that which purifies the world and destroys multitudes of major sins,
day and night dwell upon the summit of Mount Veṅkaṭa.
By the mere darśana of it, men obtain happiness of intellect.
The wives of the siddhas and cāraṇas, having made their dwelling on its summit,
worship at all times the Lord of Veṅkaṭa, the treasure-house of mercy.

Those dwelling in heaven attain liberation; those dwelling in hell attain heaven.

It exists, O brahmins, on the most meritorious and pure Mount Veṅkaṭa,

I will tell an ancient account that destroys all sins,
hearing which one is freed from all sins, there is no doubt about this.
Now, the story of the destitute brahmin named Bhadramati:
Long ago there was an eminent brahmin who had crossed to the end of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas,
a poor twice-born destitute of livelihood, named Bhadramati.
All the scriptures had been heard by that wise brahmin,
