2.1.m: Thus, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of eighty-one thousand verses, in the second Vaiṣṇava section, in the Veṅkaṭācalamāhātmya, the twenty-second chapter, entitled 'Description of the Glory of Ākāśagaṅgā'.
Now begins the māhātmya of Cakratīrtha.
Śrī Sūta said:
Now I shall tell you, O truthful lords among brahmins,
the māhātmya of Cakratīrtha, which destroys all sins.
Those who hear the most sacred glory of Cakratīrtha,
they go to the abode of Viṣṇu, from which there is no return.

2.1.s: annadāne ca vimukhā jaladāne tathaiva ca ..
2.1.d: अन्नदाने च विमुखा जलदाने तथैव च ..
2.1.m: Even those averse to the gift of food, and likewise to the gift of water,
and those averse to the gift of cows, become purified by immersion here.
Therefore, Cakratīrtha is the most sacred ford, none superior.
Now, the manner of austerity performed by the brahmin named Padmanābha:
Śrī Sūta said:
Formerly, Padmanābha of the Śrīvatsa lineage, who had conquered his senses,
performed great austerity on the bank of the Cakra pond.
Endowed with compassion, taking no food, speaking the truth, with his senses controlled,
beholding all living beings as himself, free from desire for sensory objects,
dedicated to the welfare of all beings, self-restrained, and completely free from all pairs of opposites.
For some years he subsisted on withered leaves;
for some time he lived on water alone, and for several years he consumed only air.
In this way, for twelve years, the great sage Padmanābha
Now, the manifestation of the Lord, pleased by the austerity performed at Cakra tīrtha by the twice-born named Padmanābha:
performed severe austerity, exceedingly difficult even for the gods.
Then, pleased by his austerity, the Lord, the consort of Kamalā,
bearing the conch, discus, and mace, appeared visibly before him,
with eyes like the petals of a blooming lotus, shining with a radiance equal to ten million suns.
Opening his eyes, he saw there Veṅkaṭeśvara,
tranquil, holding the conch and discus, Śrīnivāsa, a treasure of compassion.
Seeing the exalted god, he began to praise him:
Now, the praise of Śrīnivāsa offered by the twice-born named Padmanābha:
Obeisance to the supreme God of gods, to Veṅkaṭeśa who wields the bow Śārṅga!
Obeisance to you, Śrīnivāsa, who dwell upon the mountain of Nārāyaṇa!
Obeisance to Viṣṇu, to Vāsudeva, the destroyer of sins!
Obeisance to you, Śrīnivāsa, who dwell upon Śeṣācala!
Obeisance to the Lord of the three worlds, the universal-formed witness!
Obeisance to you, Śrīnivāsa, who are praised by Śiva, Brahmā, and the other gods!
Obeisance to you, the lotus-eyed, who recline upon the ocean of milk!
Obeisance to you, Śrīnivāsa, the destroyer of wicked rākṣasas!
Obeisance to the god who loves his devotees, to the Lord of gods!
Obeisance to you, Śrīnivāsa, the destroyer of the distress of those who bow!
Obeisance always to Viṣṇu, the master of yogins, knowable through the Vedas!
Obeisance to you, Śrīnivāsa, the destroyer of the sins of your devotees!
Thus praised, the illustrious Śrīnivāsa, who comprises the universe,
by the seer named Padmanābha dwelling at Cakra tīrtha,
Now, the Lord's command to Padmanābha to dwell constantly at Cakra tīrtha:
experiencing supreme satisfaction, Veṅkaṭeśa, the ocean of mercy,
to Padmanābha, the best of the twice-born, tranquil and devoted to righteousness,
spoke words resembling a stream of nectar, Puruṣottama:
Śrīnivāsa said:
O best of the twice-born, illustrious one, worshipper of my lotus feet,
dwell on the bank of Cakra tīrtha, worshipping [me] until the end of the kalpa.
Having spoken thus, the Lord Viṣṇu disappeared right there.
When the god Śrīnivāsa, the teacher of the world, had vanished,

2.1.s: cakratīrthasya tīre tu vāsaṃ cakre mahāmatiḥ ..
2.1.d: चक्रतीर्थस्य तीरे तु वासं चक्रे महामतिः ..
2.1.m: the noble-minded one took up his abode on the bank of Cakra tīrtha.
Then, after some time, a terrifying rākṣasa
approached that sage named Padmanābha, who was devoted to Nārāyaṇa;
cruel and tormented by hunger, he came to devour him.

2.1.s: brāhmaṇaṃ tarasā so'yaṃ rākṣaso jagṛhe tadā ..
2.1.d: ब्राह्मणं तरसा सोऽयं राक्षसो जगृहे तदा ..
2.1.m: Then that rākṣasa forcefully seized the brahmin.
Seized forcefully by him, the twice-born, who had mastered the Vedāṅgas,
cried out to the ocean of mercy, the refuge of the distressed,

2.1.s: nārāyaṇaṃ cakrapāṇiṃ pakṣa rakṣeti vai muhuḥ.. 27..
2.1.d: नारायणं चक्रपाणिं पक्ष रक्षेति वै मुहुः.. 27..
2.1.m: to Nārāyaṇa, the discus-bearer, saying again and again: 'Protect me! Protect me!'
O Veṅkaṭeśa, ocean of mercy, protector of those who take refuge!
Save me, O tiger among men, who have fallen under the power of a rākṣasa!
O beloved of Lakṣmī, O Hari, O Viṣṇu, O Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, whose banner is Garuḍa!

2.1.s: māṃ rakṣa rākṣasākrāṃtaṃ grāhākrāṃtaṃ gajaṃ yathā.. 29..
2.1.d: मां रक्ष राक्षसाक्रांतं ग्राहाक्रांतं गजं यथा.. 29..
2.1.m: Protect me, who am attacked by a rākṣasa, just as [you protected] the elephant seized by an alligator!
O Dāmodara, Lord of the world, slayer of the demon Hiraṇya!
Protect me, sorely afflicted by a rākṣasa, just as [you protected] Prahlāda!
Now, the dispatch of the discus by the Lord for the slaying of the demon who attempted to kill Padmanābha:
While that Padmanābha was thus praising him, O twice-born,
the discus-bearer, the treasure of compassion, knowing the danger to his devotee,
dispatched his own discus to protect his devotee.
Sent by Viṣṇu, the all-powerful Lord, that discus of Viṣṇu
then arrived swiftly at the bank of the Cakra pool.
Resembling countless suns, of equal blaze to infinite fires,
with great flames, emitting a mighty roar, the crusher of mighty demons—
seeing Viṣṇu's Sudarśana, the rākṣasa then fled.
Now, the slaying of the demon by the discus sent by the Lord:
As that rākṣasa was fleeing, Sudarśana swiftly [struck] him.
Suddenly severed the head of that running rākṣasa, [a discus] unassailable with its garland of flames. // 35

2.1.s: tato vipravaro dṛṣṭvā rākṣasaṃ patitaṃ bhuvi ..
2.1.d: ततो विप्रवरो दृष्ट्वा राक्षसं पतितं भुवि ..
2.1.m: Then the excellent brahmin, seeing the rākṣasa fallen on the ground,
Filled with supreme joy, praised Sudarśana: // 36
Padmanābha said:
O discus of Viṣṇu, praise to you, consecrated to protect the universe!
Praise to you, the ornament of Nārāyaṇa's lotus hand! // 37
Skilled in destroying asuras in battle, of mighty roar,
O Sudarśana, praise to you who destroy the distress of devotees! // 38
Protect me, agitated with fear, from every impurity.
O Master Sudarśana, all-pervading lord, may you always
Dwell in Cakratīrtha for the welfare of the world that desires liberation. // 39
Addressed thus by the brahmin, O lords of sages, that discus of Viṣṇu // 2.1.23.40
Spoke to him named Padmanābha, as though gladdening him out of affection: // 41
Now, the granting of boons and other [favors] performed by the discus at the request of the twice-born.
Sudarśana said:
O Padmanābha, highly meritorious is the unexcelled Cakratīrtha.
In it I abide constantly out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds. // 42
Considering your torment by that evil-minded rākṣasa, // 43
Dispatched by Viṣṇu, O brahmin, I arrived in haste.
And that lowest of rākṣasas who afflicted you has been slain by me. // 44

2.1.s: mocitastvaṃ bhayādasmāttvaṃ hi bhakto hareḥ sadā ..
2.1.d: मोचितस्त्वं भयादस्मात्त्वं हि भक्तो हरेः सदा ..
2.1.m: You have been freed from this fear, for you are ever a devotee of Hari.
In the highly meritorious Cakratīrtha, which takes away all sins, O twice-born, // 45
I establish my presence for you, constantly for the protection of the world.
In this [place], due to my presence, for you as well as others, O twice-born, // 46
Henceforth there will be no affliction arising from bhūtas or rākṣasas.
Due to my presence in this [place], the fame 'Cakratīrtha' will arise. // 47
Those who perform ritual ablution here in Cakratīrtha, which grants liberation,

2.1.s: teṣāṃ putrāśca pautrāśca vaṃśajāḥ sarva eva hi .. 48 ..
2.1.d: तेषां पुत्राश्च पौत्राश्च वंशजाः सर्व एव हि .. 48 ..
2.1.m: Their sons, grandsons, and all born in their lineage indeed, // 48
Cleansed of sin, will go to that supreme abode of Viṣṇu.
Having spoken thus, that discus of Viṣṇu, while Padmanābha watched // 49
And while other brahmins also watched, suddenly, O twice-born,
Entered that Cakra pond which destroys sins. // 2.1.23.50
Glorious Sūta said:
The sin-destroying māhātmya of Cakratīrtha,
Has all been recounted to you, O foremost brahmins, Śaunaka and others of great splendor. // 51

2.1.s: cakratīrthasamaṃ tīrthaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati ..
2.1.d: चक्रतीर्थसमं तीर्थं न भूतं न भविष्यति ..
2.1.m: A sacred ford equal to Cakratīrtha never was, nor will ever be.

2.1.s: atra snātvā narā viprā mokṣabhājo na saṃśayaḥ ..92 ..
2.1.d: अत्र स्नात्वा नरा विप्रा मोक्षभाजो न संशयः ..92 ..
2.1.m: Having bathed here, men become partakers of liberation, O brahmins, without a doubt. // 52
Whoever proclaims this chapter or hears it with concentrated mind
Obtains the excellent fruit of bathing in Cakratīrtha. // 53

2.1.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīveṃkaṭācalamāhātmye cakratīrthamahimānuvarṇanaṃnāma trayoviṃśatitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 23 ..
2.1.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीवेंकटाचलमाहात्म्ये चक्रतीर्थमहिमानुवर्णनंनाम त्रयोविंशतितमोऽध्यायः .. 23 ..
2.1.m: Thus ends the twenty-third chapter, named 'Description of the Glory of Cakratīrtha,' in the Śrī Veṃkaṭācala-māhātmya in the second Vaiṣṇava section of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. // 23
Now begins the account of the attainment and cessation of the state of a rākṣasa by the gandharva named Sundara.
The seers said:
O venerable Sūta, foremost of Purāṇa reciters, who was that rākṣasa
Who oppressed that high-souled brahmin devotee of Viṣṇu? // 1
Glorious Sūta said:

2.1.s: vakṣyāmi rākṣasaṃ krūraṃ taṃ viprāḥ śṛṇutādarāt ..
2.1.d: वक्ष्यामि राक्षसं क्रूरं तं विप्राः शृणुतादरात् ..
2.1.m: I shall tell of that cruel rākṣasa; listen attentively, O brahmins,

2.1.s: yathā ca rākṣaso jāto munīnāṃ śāpavaibhavāt .. 2 ..
2.1.d: यथा च राक्षसो जातो मुनीनां शापवैभवात् .. 2 ..
2.1.m: And how he was born a rākṣasa by the power of the sages' curse. // 2
Formerly, in Śrīraṅga, the abode of Viṣṇu that resembles Vaikuṇṭha,
All the devotees of Viṣṇu of great splendor, headed by Vasiṣṭha and Atri, // 3
Dwelling in the city of Śrīraṅga, for the sake of liberation,
Worshiped Śrīraṅganātha, the lord of gods, who grants fearlessness to his devotees. // 4
Once, a powerful gandharva there, the son of Vīrabāhu,
Named Sundara, O foremost brahmins, devoted to the company of rakes, // 5
Accompanied by a hundred women, naked in a pool of water,
Sported joyfully together with those naked young women. // 6
At the sacred ford of the daughter of Kavera, Vasiṣṭha, along with the sages,
Intending to perform the midday rites, went out from the Śrīraṅga temple. // 7
Then, seeing those seers, those women, distressed by fear,
Covered themselves with garments; but not the reckless Sundara. // 8
Thereupon Vasiṣṭha, enraged, cursed that shameless one: // 9
Vasiṣṭha said:
“Since, O Gandharva Sundara, on seeing us, you did not, out of shame,

2.1.s: vāso nācchāditaṃ śīghraṃ yāhi rākṣasatāṃ tataḥ .. 2.1.24.10 ..
2.1.m: cover yourself with a garment, quickly attain the state of a rākṣasa on that account!”
When this was spoken by Vasiṣṭha, the women, with folded hands,
bowing down to Vasiṣṭha with hearts humbled by devotion,
said this to Vasiṣṭha in the midst of the circle of sages:
The women said:
“O blessed one, knower of all righteousness, son of the four-faced [Brahmā]!
O ocean of compassion, looking upon us, you ought not to be angry.
For a husband alone is said to be the supreme ornament of women.

2.1.s: patihīnā tu yā nārī śataputrāpi sā mune .. .. 14 ..
2.1.d: पतिहीना तु या नारी शतपुत्रापि सा मुने .. .. 14 ..
2.1.m: Even a woman with a hundred sons, O sage, if bereft of a husband,
is called a widow in the world; their life is utterly in vain.
Therefore, show grace, O sage, out of respect, toward our husband.
A single offense should be forgiven by sages who see the truth.
Extend forgiveness, O ocean of compassion, to Sundara here, who is your pupil.”
Śrī Sūta said:
Vasiṣṭha, being thus implored by the women of Sundara,

2.1.s: provāca vacanaṃ bhūyaḥ prasannaḥ sa dvijottamaḥ .. 17 ..
2.1.d: प्रोवाच वचनं भूयः प्रसन्नः स द्विजोत्तमः .. 17 ..
2.1.m: spoke these words once more, pleased, that best of the twice-born:
Now the means spoken by Vasiṣṭha for the end of the state of a rākṣasa of the one named Sundara:
Vasiṣṭha said:

2.1.s: na me syādvacanaṃ mithyā kadācidapi subhruvaḥ ..
2.1.d: न मे स्याद्वचनं मिथ्या कदाचिदपि सुभ्रुवः ..
2.1.m: “My word can never be false, O fair-browed ones.

2.1.s: upāyaṃ vaḥ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇudhvaṃ śraddhayā saha .. 18 ..
2.1.d: उपायं वः प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणुध्वं श्रद्धया सह .. 18 ..
2.1.m: I shall tell you a remedy; listen with faith.
The curse on your husband will certainly have a duration of sixteen years.
And at the end of the sixteen-year limit, Sundara, possessing the form of a rākṣasa,
by chance [reaching] the auspicious Veṅkaṭa mountain that removes all sins,
having gone [there], O celestial women, will reach that Cakratīrtha.
There dwells Padmanābha, a great yogin and lord of sages.
This rākṣasa will approach that sage in order to devour him.
Then, dispatched for the protection of the brahmin, the excellent discus
will sever his head from his body by Viṣṇu, no doubt.

2.1.s: tataḥ svaṃ rūpamāsādya śāpānmuktaḥ sa sundaraḥ ..
2.1.d: ततः स्वं रूपमासाद्य शापान्मुक्तः स सुन्दरः ..
2.1.m: Then, having regained his own form and being freed from the curse, that Sundara,
your husband, will go to heaven once more; there is no doubt about this.
Then, having reached heaven, this Sundara, your husband,
wearing a beautiful attire, will delight you, O beautiful ones!”
Śrī Sūta said:
Having spoken thus to those excellent women of Sundara, Vasiṣṭha,
devoted to the lord Śrīraṅga, quickly departed to his own hermitage.
Then the women, embracing him, Sundara, their husband,
wept, tormented by grief, plunged into the midst of an ocean of sorrow.
While they were thus watching, Sundara became a rākṣasa,
with huge fangs, a massive body, and red beard and hair on his head.
Seeing him, agitated with fear, the women went to heaven.
Then this one disguised as a rākṣasa, [formerly] Sundara, terrifying in appearance,
devouring all living beings, from region to region, from forest to forest,
wandering with the speed of the wind, [arrived at] the excellent mountain, Veṅkaṭādri.
Having entered it, that great sinner then went to Cakratīrtha.
In this way sixteen years passed for him as he wandered.
Then, at the end of the sixteen years, O lords of sages, this rākṣasa,
in order to devour that Padmanābha, the dweller at Cakratīrtha,
rushed with the speed of the wind; and he [the sage] praised Janārdana.
And Viṣṇu, praised by the yogin, then dispatched his discus
to protect that Padmanābha who was oppressed by the rākṣasa.
Then, arriving, Hari's discus severed the head of the rākṣasa.
Now the attainment of his own true form preceded by the release from the state of a rākṣasa of the one named Sundara:
Then he, abandoning the rākṣasa body, having an ethereal form,
mounting an excellent vimāna, Sundara, showered with flowers,
having folded his hands and bowed down, paid homage to that Sudarśana.
He praised it with foremost words, pleasing to the ear, with reverence:
Sundara said:
“O Sudarśana, salutations unto you, sole ornament of Viṣṇu’s hand!
Homage to you, destroyer of the asuras, possessed of the radiance of a thousand suns!
Through an influx of your grace, casting off my rākṣasa body,
I have attained my own form. O discus weapon of Viṣṇu, homage to you!
Permit me to go to heaven, O beloved of Viṣṇu;
My wives are grieving, their hearts anguished by separation.
As long as I live, may my mind remain fixed on you;

2.1.s: tathā rūpaṃ kuruṣva tvaṃ mayi cakra namo'stu te .. 39 ..
2.1.d: तथा रूपं कुरुष्व त्वं मयि चक्र नमोऽस्तु ते .. 39 ..
2.1.m: Grant such a state to me, O discus! Homage to you!"
Thus praised with devotion by Sundara,
Viṣṇu's discus at once granted him [his prayer], saying, "May it be so," O lords of sages.
Having received permission from the discus weapon, Sundara bowed down to the best of brahmins;
Permitted by him, the gandharva went to heaven.

2.1.s: sundare tu gate svargaṃ padmanābho munīśvaraḥ ..
2.1.d: सुन्दरे तु गते स्वर्गं पद्मनाभो मुनीश्वरः ..
2.1.m: And when Sundara had gone to heaven, Padmanābha, the lord among sages,
Prayed to that discus: "O weapon of Viṣṇu, homage to you!
O discus weapon, crusher of great asuras, I bow to you.
Establish your presence in this pure, auspicious Cakra tīrtha.
Through your presence, for all sinners who bathe here,

2.1.s: pāpanāśaṃ kuruṣva tvaṃ mokṣaṃ ca kuru śāśvatam .. 44 ..
2.1.d: पापनाशं कुरुष्व त्वं मोक्षं च कुरु शाश्वतम् .. 44 ..
2.1.m: Bring about the destruction of sin, and grant eternal liberation.
Establish its renown in the world as 'Cakratīrtha.'
Through your presence, may the destruction of fear for the sages residing here

2.1.s: itaḥ paraṃ bhavatvārya cakrāyudha namo'stu te ..
2.1.d: इतः परं भवत्वार्य चक्रायुध नमोऽस्तु ते ..
2.1.m: Be effected henceforth, O noble one! O discus weapon, homage to you!
Let there be no fear of bhūtas, pretas, and piśācas, O Lord!"
When prayed to in this manner by the yogin Padmanābha,
The discus replied, "May it indeed be so," and vanished into that sacred ford.
Śrī Sūta said:

2.1.s: evaṃ vaḥ kathitaṃ viprā rākṣasasyodbhave mayā ..
2.1.d: एवं वः कथितं विप्रा राक्षसस्योद्भवे मया ..
2.1.m: Thus, O brahmins, on the occasion of the rākṣasa's origin, has been told to you by me
The māhātmya of Cakratīrtha, which removes impurity,
Hearing which a mortal is freed from all sins on earth.

2.1.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīveṃkaṭācalamāhātmye cakratīrthamahimānuvarṇanaṃnāma caturviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 24 ..
2.1.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीवेंकटाचलमाहात्म्ये चक्रतीर्थमहिमानुवर्णनंनाम चतुर्विंशोऽध्यायः .. 24 ..
2.1.m: Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, titled "Description of the Greatness of Cakratīrtha," in the Śrīveṅkaṭācalamāhātmya of the second [section], the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Now begins the description of the māhātmya of Jābālitīrtha.
Śrī Sūta said:
"O all you whose wealth is austerity, dwellers of Naimiṣāraṇya!
On the holy Veṅkaṭa mountain, the destroyer of all sins,
I shall now describe the māhātmya of Jābālitīrtha,
Where, having bathed, a [brahmin] named Durācāra became liberated, O twice-born ones."
The sages said:
"Who was this one named Durācāra, O Sūta, knower of true principles?

2.1.s: kiñca pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ tena durācāreṇa vai mune .. 3 ..
2.1.d: किञ्च पापं कृतं तेन दुराचारेण वै मुने .. 3 ..
2.1.m: And what sin was committed by that Durācāra, O sage?
Or how was he freed from his sin by the power of bathing in this sacred ford?
Tell this to us in detail, as we wish to hear it, O sage."
Now begins the account of the twice-born named Durācāra who lived on the bank of the Kāverī.
Śrī Sūta said:
"O sages, hear the sin of that Durācāra,
And how he was freed from the sin by bathing in Jābālitīrtha.
There was a certain sinful twice-born named Durācāra,
A brahmin who lived on the bank of the Kāverī, ever engaged in cruel deeds.
Corrupted by continual association with killers of brahmins, drinkers of liquor,
Thieves, and defilers of the Guru's bed, he lived with them, O twice-born ones.
By the fault of association with those who commit great sins,
All the brahminhood of this twice-born was completely destroyed, O best of the twice-born.

2.1.s: mahāpātakibhiḥ sārdhaṃ dinamekaṃ tu yo dvijaḥ ..
2.1.d: महापातकिभिः सार्धं दिनमेकं तु यो द्विजः ..
2.1.m: Whatever twice-born should dwell respectfully for even a single day
With perpetrators of great sins, from that very moment, of that twice-born,

2.1.s: brāhmaṇasya tu caikāṃśo naśyatyeva na saṃśayaḥ ..
2.1.d: ब्राह्मणस्य तु चैकांशो नश्यत्येव न संशयः ..
2.1.m: One part of his brahminhood is indeed destroyed—there is no doubt.
From serving, touching, seeing, or sleeping [with them] for two days,
And from eating in the same row with perpetrators of great sins, O twice-born ones,
The second part of his brahminhood would be destroyed—there is no doubt.
From three days, the third part is indeed destroyed—there is no doubt;
And from four days, the fourth part certainly dissolves away.

2.1.s: ataḥ paraṃ ca taiḥ sākaṃ śayanāsanabhojanaiḥ ..
2.1.d: अतः परं च तैः साकं शयनासनभोजनैः ..
2.1.m: Beyond that, by sleeping, sitting, and dining together with them,
He who associates with perpetrators of great sins becomes an equal sinner to them.
Therefore, this twice-born named Durācāra was bereft of brahminhood...
was seized, as if by a mighty, terrifying serpent.
Fallen under its control and exceedingly tormented by that vetāla,
that brahmin wandered from country to country and from forest to forest.
Through the ripening of former merit and the working of destiny, that brahmin,
[came to] Mount Veṅkaṭa, supremely meritorious and destroying all sins.
Now, the release of Durācāra and the vetāla from the mortal sins and other [evils] through ritual ablution in the Jābālitīrtha.
Pursued by the piśāca, the vetāla, the brahmin reached [it].
That vetāla submerged him into the destroyer of mortal sins,
into the Jābālitīrtha, O foremost brahmins, [the brahmin] who had associated with a mortal sinner.
In that very instant he arose, freed by the vetāla.
Having emerged from that purifying sacred ford, O brahmins,
restored to health, that brahmin reflected: “What is this [mountain] near the Svarṇamukhī?
Oh, how have I, an inhabitant of the banks of the Kāverī, come here?”
Disturbed by this thought, [seeing] that excellent sacred ford of Jābāli
and the great-souled Jābāli, the best and highest of lordly yogins,
that Durācāra approached, bowed down, and spoke:
“O venerable brahmin, I do not know this mountain; tell me now!
I am indeed an inhabitant of the bank of the Kāverī, named Durācāra.
Out of compassion, tell me, O brahmin: how did I come here?”
Thus questioned by that Durācāra, the sage of good vows,
that treasure-house of compassion, meditated for a moment and spoke to Durācāra.
Now, the recounting of the fault of not performing the pārvaṇa-śrāddha, as related by Jābāli.
Jābāli said:
“Because of your association with a mortal sinner, O Durācāra, in the past,
your brahminhood was lost; then a vetāla seized you.
Possessed by him, bewildered in mind and helpless, you came here.
The vetāla submerged you in this exceedingly purifying sacred ford.
By mere immersion here, you have been freed from sin.

2.1.s: jābālitīrthe ye snānaṃ puṇyaṃ kurvanti mānavāḥ.. 27..
2.1.d: जाबालितीर्थे ये स्नानं पुण्यं कुर्वन्ति मानवाः.. 27..
2.1.m: Those mortals who perform a meritorious ritual ablution in the Jābālitīrtha,
their accumulated five mortal sins are truly destroyed.
By merely bathing in this meritorious sacred ford, an instrument for good deeds,
your guilt arising from contact with a mortal sinner has dissolved.
The vetāla who seized you was previously a brahmin.
He did not perform the ancestral śrāddha on the day of death with the pārvaṇa rite.
Cursed by his own ancestors because of that, he attained the state of a vetāla.
Even he, through the power of ritual ablution in the waters of the Jābālitīrtha,
abandoned the state of a vetāla and attained the world of Viṣṇu.
A man who does not perform the śrāddha on the day of his parents' death,
quickly reaches the state of a vetāla and afterward experiences hell.”
Śrī Sūta said:
Even that great sinner Durācāra, by merely bathing in this sacred ford,
attained the world of Viṣṇu, from which there is no return.
Thus the meritorious deliverance of Durācāra has been related to you.
Therefore it is the most meritorious, auspicious sacred ford, removing all sins,
where Durācāra was delivered by merely bathing.
It destroys even those sins for which there is no expiation.

2.1.s: śūdreṇa pūjitaṃ liṅgaṃ viṣṇuṃ vā yo nameddvijaḥ ..
2.1.d: शूद्रेण पूजितं लिङ्गं विष्णुं वा यो नमेद्द्विजः ..
2.1.m: If a brahmin bows to a liṅga or to Viṣṇu worshipped by a Śūdra,
no expiation is prescribed for him in the smṛtis by the supreme seers;
yet even that sin of his is destroyed in the sacred ford named Jābāli.
And for those who revile brahmins, no expiation is found;
for betrayers of trust and ungrateful people, no expiation,
and for those engaged with a brother’s wife, no expiation is found.
For them, purification will surely come from ritual ablution in the Jābālitīrtha.
Thus the grandeur of the sacred ford of Jābāli has been recounted to you, O brahmins,
hearing which a mortal on earth is liberated from all sins.

2.1.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīveṃkaṭācalamāhātmye jābālitīrthamahimānuvarṇanaṃnāma pañcaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 25 ..
2.1.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीवेंकटाचलमाहात्म्ये जाबालितीर्थमहिमानुवर्णनंनाम पञ्चविंशोऽध्यायः .. 25 ..
2.1.m: Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, entitled “Description of the Greatness of the Jābālitīrtha,” in the Venkaṭācalamāhātmya in the second section, the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, of the glorious Skandamahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Now, the greatness of the Tumburu (Ghoṇa) sacred ford.
Śrī Sūta said:
“Here I shall proclaim, O Śaunaka and other [sages] of great splendour,
the māhātmya of the Ghoṇatīrtha, which destroys all sins.”
For people, a ritual ablution there yields the fruit of austerities performed in another birth.
On the full moon festival day of the bright fortnight conjoined with Uttarāphalgunī,
when the sun resides in Pisces, all the sacred fords everywhere,
the Gaṅgā and others in the three worlds, arrive in the afternoon at Tumbu's sacred ford.
The seers said: / O venerable Sūta, omniscient one, master of the meaning of all sacred treatises,
all the rivers beginning with Gaṅgā, at the exceedingly purifying Ghoṇatīrtha—

2.1.s: kimarthaṃ snāṃti vai tatra mīnasaṃsthe prabhākare .. 5 ..
2.1.d: किमर्थं स्नांति वै तत्र मीनसंस्थे प्रभाकरे .. 5 ..
2.1.m: for what purpose do they perform ritual ablution there when the sun resides in Pisces?
The venerable Sūta said:

2.1.s: pāpino manujāḥ sarve hyasmāsu snānti yatnataḥ ..
2.1.d: पापिनो मनुजाः सर्वे ह्यस्मासु स्नान्ति यत्नतः ..
2.1.m: "Indeed, all sinful mortals diligently bathe in us;

2.1.s: visṛjya pāpajālāni kṛtārthā yāṃti vai janāḥ .. 6 ..
2.1.d: विसृज्य पापजालानि कृतार्था यांति वै जनाः .. 6 ..
2.1.m: casting off their webs of sin, people depart fulfilled.
How can that web of our sins be completely destroyed?"
Having thus reflected, the sacred fords headed by Gaṅgā, with great effort,
remembering the enchanting and divine speech of the great-souled Nārada,
the son of Brahmā, which eradicates all sins,
having gone to Mount Śrīveṅkaṭa, which dries up [sins such as] the murder of a brahmin,
and having bathed there in the waters of the Svāmipuṣkariṇī, the foremost of sacred fords,
thereafter, O brahmins, at the exceedingly purifying Ghoṇatīrtha,
on the festival day of the bright fortnight conjoined with Uttarāphalgunī,
all the sacred fords bathe when the sun resides in Pisces.

2.1.s: tasya tīrthasya māhātmyaṃ ko vetti bhuvanatraye .. 11 ..
2.1.d: तस्य तीर्थस्य माहात्म्यं को वेत्ति भुवनत्रये .. 11 ..
2.1.m: Who in the three worlds knows the greatness of that sacred ford?
Now the description of the great faults of those averse to bathing in Ghoṇatīrtha:
Therefore, O best of the twice-born, Ghoṇatīrtha is the most sacred of sacred fords.
One who destroys groves, is cruel, sells daughters and horses,
and has abandoned the bath at Ghoṇa—they call him a murderer of a brahmin.
One who plunders property of the gods as well as one who seizes what was given,
and has abandoned the bath at Ghoṇa—they call him a murderer of a brahmin.
One who breaches reservoirs and dams, one who lusts after intercourse with another's wife,
and has abandoned the bath at Ghoṇa—the wise call him a thief.
That vile materialist who, having said to a twice-born, "I give,"
[does not,] and has abandoned the bath at Ghoṇa—the wise know him as a drinker of liquor.
One who is hostile to gurus and twice-born folk, devoted to self-praise,
and has abandoned the bath at Ghoṇa—the wise call him a thief.
One who eats unconsecrated food, one who consumes food left over from ancestral rites,
and has abandoned the bath at Ghoṇa—the twice-born call him a thief.
One who gives food left over from ancestral rites [to others], one who opposes mother and father,
and has abandoned the bath at Ghoṇa—the wise call him a thief.
One intent on union with another's wife, fond of pleasure with a brother's wife,
and has abandoned the bath at Ghoṇa—they call him a violator of the guru's bed.
A twice-born who speaks with an outcaste, who constantly lacks kuśa grass in hand,
and has abandoned the bath at Ghoṇa—contact with him is indeed the fifth [great sin].
One who eats food after hearing the voice of a menstruating woman, a dog, or an outcaste,
and has abandoned the bath at Ghoṇa—contact with him is indeed the fifth [great sin].
One who causes obstacles to the Purāṇas, marriages, sacred thread ceremonies, and other religious duties,
and has abandoned the bath at Ghoṇa—they call him a slaughterer of cattle.
One who slays someone who has sought refuge, one turned away from all sacred fords,
and has abandoned the bath at Ghoṇa—the wise call him a killer of an embryo.
One who has neglected ancestral sacrifices, abandoned his wife, the lowest of his lineage,
and has abandoned the bath at Ghoṇa—they call him a killer of cows.
The minor sins that are equal to great sins,
O best of the twice-born, attach to one who has abandoned the bath at Ghoṇa.
Now the description of the removal of all sins by the bath at Ghoṇa:
O brahmins, even one addicted to great sins, a dog-cooker or the lowest of his family,
cruel, a destroyer of his lineage, miserable, ungenerous, devoid of righteous rites,
a slayer of animals, devoted to hostility toward others, and likewise a slanderer,
a speaker of untruth, deceitful, and attached to another's wife,
a betrayer of friends, an ungrateful man, a killer of an embryo, and an extreme sinner,
delighting in another's wife, wicked, an informant regarding others' wealth,
false, engaged in agriculture, treacherous to his master, and a deceiver,
greedy, a killer of his father, turned away from all gods,
praising himself, creating obstacles to righteousness, dishonest—
the one who spends wealth on the unworthy, who breaks up harmony,
the cutter of trees endowed with fine shoots and fruits,
the betrayer of trust, and the one devoted to slaying warriors,
one who maintains no sacred fire, who has no son, one who employs poison,
one who hates the guru, the sinner who brings discord between husband and wife,
one who exercises lordship over a village or likewise over a temple,
a brahmin who makes a display for hire, one intent on cruel deeds,
one who has made a habit of a multitude of sins, one devoted to secret vices,
one who commits sin through ignorance, or who does wicked deeds knowingly—
all these, O foremost of brahmins, the charming Ghoṇatīrtha
purifies through ritual ablution, drinking, and the like. Ah, the grandeur of the sacred ford! // 36
Now begins the story of the gandharva named Tumburu.
Śrī Sūta said:
Here I shall relate an ancient legend, destroying sin,
calming all evils, bestowing the fruit of liberation. // 37
Formerly, Gārgya, endowed with great splendor, skilled in all branches of learning,
all-knowing, moral, a brahmin of controlled senses, spoke thus: // 38
Bowing to the great-souled Devala, his mind serene, [he said:]
“Relate [it], O fortunate one; be compassionate to me!
Tell of the auspicious māhātmya of Ghoṇatīrtha, which takes away all sins.” // 39
Devala said:
A gandharva named Tumburu, having cursed his devoted wife,
bathed here and worshipped Veṅkaṭeśa, the ocean of mercy, // 40
and attained the realm of Viṣṇu, free from return [to rebirth]. // 41
Gārgya said:

2.1.s: kimarthaṃ devala ṛṣe bhāryāṃ rūpavatīṃ striyam ..
2.1.d: किमर्थं देवल ऋषे भार्यां रूपवतीं स्त्रियम् ..
2.1.m: “For what reason, O seer Devala, did the gandharva named Tumburu,
skilled in all branches of learning, // 42
curse his beautiful wife, a woman endowed with all virtues? By what fault [did this happen]?

2.1.s: tadvadasva mahābhāga śrotuṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me .. 43 ..
2.1.d: तद्वदस्व महाभाग श्रोतुं कौतूहलं हि मे .. 43 ..
2.1.m: Tell that, O fortunate one, for my curiosity to hear is great.” // 43
Now begins the manner of the rule of the Māgha ablution taught by Tumburu to his wife.

2.1.s: tumbururnāma gandharvo bhāryāṃ prītyā hyuvāca ha ..
2.1.d: तुम्बुरुर्नाम गन्धर्वो भार्यां प्रीत्या ह्युवाच ह ..
2.1.m: The gandharva named Tumburu spoke lovingly to his wife:

2.1.s: māghatraye mayā sākaṃ snānaṃ kuru malāpaham .. .. 44 ..
2.1.d: माघत्रये मया साकं स्नानं कुरु मलापहम् .. .. 44 ..
2.1.m: “Perform with me the bath that removes impurities during the three [critical days of] Māgha. // 44
In the month of Māgha, when the sun has risen, destroying all sins,
smear this bank with cow dung for the worship of Viṣṇu. // 45
With colored powders and minerals, [draw] white lotuses and svastikas.
Serve me and Viṣṇu in this auspicious month. // 46
In this Māgha, prepare a lamp-wick for this Mādhava;

2.1.s: sadhūpaṃ pāvakaṃ bhaktyā samarpaya hareḥ puraḥ .. 47 ..
2.1.d: सधूपं पावकं भक्त्या समर्पय हरेः पुरः .. 47 ..
2.1.m: with devotion offer before Hari fire along with incense. // 47
Having become pure, cook food for the great-souled Mādhava.
With circumambulations and prostrations, with devotion along with me in Māgha, // 48
perform daily worship to Viṣṇu, the God of gods.
Unwearied, listen constantly to the Purāṇa of Viṣṇu. // 49

2.1.s: nityaṃ snātvā prayatnena piba pādodakaṃ hareḥ ..
2.1.d: नित्यं स्नात्वा प्रयत्नेन पिब पादोदकं हरेः ..
2.1.m: Having bathed every day, drink with diligence Hari's foot-water.
‘Kṛṣṇa! Viṣṇu! Mukunda! Nārāyaṇa! Janārdana! // 50
Acyuta! Ananta! Soul of all!’—chant thus unceasingly.
Abandoning anger, jealousy, greed, and the like, observe the vow. // 51
Thereby liberation will be yours, and the eternal realm of Viṣṇu.”
Now begins the manner of the curse given by Tumburu to his wife and the liberation from it.
Hearing what her husband said thus, the gandharva's beloved,
in anger, spoke unbearable [words] to her husband that lead to misfortune: // 52
“When intense cold has arisen in Māgha, and the sun has risen faintly in the morning,
how could one plunge into [water] in this Māgha that brings torment from cold, O sinless one? // 53
The rites mentioned by you cannot be performed by me repeatedly.

2.1.s: na karomi pate snānaṃ prātaḥkāle tvayā saha .. 54 ..
2.1.d: न करोमि पते स्नानं प्रातःकाले त्वया सह .. 54 ..
2.1.m: O husband, I will not take a bath with you in the morning. // 54

2.1.s: mṛtau śītātipātena na ca me rakṣako bhavān ..
2.1.d: मृतौ शीतातिपातेन न च मे रक्षको भवान् ..
2.1.m: If I die from extreme cold, you will not be my protector!”
Hearing what was spoken thus, her husband, the gandharva lord, // 55
though peaceful, then cursed his wife who spoke unpleasant words.
A son averse to righteousness, a wife who speaks unpleasant words, // 56

2.1.s: abrahmaṇyaṃ ca rājānaṃ sadyaḥ śāpena daṇḍayet ..
2.1.d: अब्रह्मण्यं च राजानं सद्यः शापेन दण्डयेत् ..
2.1.m: and a king hostile to brahmins—one should punish them immediately with a curse.

2.1.s: iti nyāyaṃ viciṃtyāsau śaśāpetthaṃ satīṃ tadā .. 57 ..
2.1.d: इति न्यायं विचिंत्यासौ शशापेत्थं सतीं तदा .. 57 ..
2.1.m: Considering this maxim, he then cursed the faithful wife thus: // 57
"On the highly meritorious Veṅkaṭādri, which destroys all sins,
and near Ghoṇatīrtha, inside the hollow of a pippala tree,
there, devoid of water, O foolish woman, become merely a frog!"
Hearing such words of her husband, the beloved of the gandharva,
falling at his feet, the chaste woman begged Tumburu.
Her husband Tumburu then declared the counter-curse:
"Indeed, Agastya, the greatly fortunate ascetic whose senses are conquered,
having bathed in the excellent Ghoṇatīrtha on the great lunar day of the full moon,
when, beside that aśvattha tree, to his disciples
the best of brahmins speaks the māhātmya of Ghoṇatīrtha,
then you, attentive inside the hollow of the pippala tree,
having heard the liberation-granting māhātmya of Ghoṇatīrtha,
having shaken off all sins, will delight with me."
Thus addressed, the lawful, faithful wife then fell silent.
From her husband's curse, she entered the most terrible body of a frog.
On that summit of Śeṣādri, to the south of Ghoṇatīrtha,
the woman went very slowly into the hollow of the pippala tree.
Ten thousand years passed for her inside the hollow of the aśvattha tree.
Then, after a period of time, Agastya went to the enchanting Veṅkaṭādri,
and, having bathed according to the rules in the sacred Śrīsvāmitīrtha,
having bowed to the god Varāhasvāmin to the south of the sacred ford,
having gone to the abode of Veṅkaṭeśa, to Śrīnivāsa, the treasure-house of compassion,
to the eternal God of gods, whose eyes are large, who is known through the Vedas,
having bowed down, the greatly fortunate Agastya then went to Ghoṇatīrtha.

2.1.s: tatra snātvā tīrthavarye svaśiṣyai yogināṃ varaḥ ..
2.1.d: तत्र स्नात्वा तीर्थवर्ये स्वशिष्यै योगिनां वरः ..
2.1.m: Having bathed there in that best of sacred fords with his disciples, the best of yogins,
under the shade of the pippala tree, with devotion to his disciples,
the māhātmya of Ghoṇatīrtha, which destroys the murder of a brahmin,
bestows all auspiciousness, is meritorious, and grants all prosperities,
the foremost among yogins, the blessed seer Agastya, proclaimed.

2.1.s: .. atha ghoṇatīrthe agastyadarśanena tumburupatnyā varṣābhūtva nivṛttiḥ .. ..
2.1.d: .. अथ घोणतीर्थे अगस्त्यदर्शनेन तुम्बुरुपत्न्या वर्षाभूत्व निवृत्तिः .. ..
2.1.m: Now, at Ghoṇatīrtha, through the darśana of Agastya, the cessation of Tumburu's wife's state as a frog:

2.1.s: tadā śrutvā tu varṣābhūḥ pādayostasya yoginaḥ ..
2.1.d: तदा श्रुत्वा तु वर्षाभूः पादयोस्तस्य योगिनः ..
2.1.m: Then, having heard [it], the female frog, at the feet of that yogin
fell, having perceived the glory of the sage through the lamp of knowledge.
Having attained her former form, the captivating form of a woman,
"O Agastya, foremost of yogins, protect, protect, O ocean of mercy!
Protect me with compassion, O brahmin, who opposed the words of her husband!"

2.1.s: ityuktvā taṃ vikṣālākṣī virarāma tataḥ param .. 75 ..
2.1.d: इत्युक्त्वा तं विक्षालाक्षी विरराम ततः परम् .. 75 ..
2.1.m: Having said this to him, the large-eyed woman then fell silent.
Agastya said:

2.1.s: kā tvaṃ suśroṇi bhadraṃ te bhekajanmapradāyakam ..
2.1.d: का त्वं सुश्रोणि भद्रं ते भेकजन्मप्रदायकम् ..
2.1.m: "Who are you, O fair-hipped lady? May there be auspiciousness to you. What sin in a previous birth

2.1.s: pāpaṃ pūrvabhave cāsīttadvadasva ca mā ciram ..76..
2.1.d: पापं पूर्वभवे चासीत्तद्वदस्व च मा चिरम् ..76..
2.1.m: bestowed the birth of a frog? Tell that, and do not delay."
The woman said:

Now, the determination of the times for bathing in the six sacred fords beginning with Svāmipuṣkariṇī:

Svāmipuṣkariṇī, and after that Viyadgaṅgā;
then Pāpavināśa, and next Pāṇḍutīrtha;
the Kumāradhārikātīrtha, and after that the sacred ford of Tumburu.

2.1.m: the knower of the Purāṇa is always to be saluted; he is to be honored by those of good deeds.
One should never form a low opinion of a knower of the Purāṇa,

To those who sink down having been born again and again in thousands of crores of existences,

When the Purāṇa-reciting brahmin has mounted the seat of Vyāsa,
he should not bow to anyone until the conclusion of the discourse.
Not in a place crowded with wicked people, not in one surrounded by Śūdras and beasts,
not in a gambling hall, should the wise man speak the meritorious narrative.
In a good village crowded with good people, in a good sacred field, in a temple of a deity,
or on a holy riverbank, the wise man should speak the meritorious narrative.
Endowed with faith and devotion, having no longing for other matters,

Now begins the māhātmya of Kaṭāhatīrtha.
The seers said:
O Sūta, knower of the true nature of all things, master of the Vedas and Vedānta!
On the glorious Veṅkaṭa mountain is a most purifying sacred ford named Kaṭāha. (1)

2.1.s: śrūyate tasya māhātmyaṃ ghuṣyate ca jagattraye ..
2.1.d: श्रूयते तस्य माहात्म्यं घुष्यते च जगत्त्रये ..
2.1.m: Its māhātmya is heard about and proclaimed in the three worlds.
O you who were instructed by Vyāsa, tell this to us out of compassion! (2)
Formerly indeed, the glorious Nārada, son of Brahmā and great seer,
that best of the twice-born, having seen the Naimiṣa forest, arrived [there]. (3)
Then, having worshipped that son of Brahmā in the proper manner with auspicious water for arghya, pādya, and the rest,
and having seated him upon a pure seat of kuśa grass, (4)
with great devotion, their necks bowed down in humility,
having bowed, all these great seers petitioned him: (5)
Except for you, O glorious Nārada, in the three worlds
there is no teacher of dharma among the great seers—none at all! (6)
On the holy Veṅkaṭa mountain, served by all the gods,
divine, descended from Vaikuṇṭha, frequented by Siddhas and Gandharvas, (7)
describe today the māhātmya of the Kaṭāhatīrtha to the forest-dwellers! (8)
The glorious Nārada said:
Listen, all you seers headed by Śaunaka, endowed with great splendor!
Who in the three worlds knows the māhātmya of the Kaṭāhatīrtha? (9)
Mahādeva knows the majesty of that sacred ford.

Praise of that sacred ford in the Śrutis, Smṛtis, and Purāṇas .. 14 ..

most wonderful, O brahmins, the sole purifier of all worlds. .. 15 ..
Even ten thousand murders of brahmins, and likewise ten thousand instances of drinking liquor,
ten thousand violations of the guru's bed that bring about sin, .. 16 ..

Whatever diverse sins there are that are without expiation,
all of them are destroyed by resorting to this sacred ford. .. 18 ..
This sacred ford is exceedingly holy, issuing from the Lord's feet.
Whoever, afflicted with leprosy or other diseases, drinks this every day .. 19 ..

even he, freed from disease, goes to the realm of Viṣṇu.
In ancient times the Lord, the divine Śaṃkara, in a secret realization, .. 2.1.28.20 ..
related the majesty of that sacred ford to Pārvatī.
No doubt should ever be entertained concerning these statements; .. 21 ..
nor should it ever be said that this is mere eulogy.
Those atheistic souls who say this is mere eulogy— .. 22 ..

Now, the method of drinking [the water of] the Kaṭāhatīrtha.
Śrī Sūta said:
O all you whose wealth is austerity, dwellers in the Naimiṣa forest,
hear the māhātmya of the Kaṭāhatīrtha, O best of the twice-born! .. 28 ..

2.1.m: The Kaṭāhatīrtha, O brahmins, is renowned in all worlds,
bestowing all prosperity, pure, the destroyer of all sins. .. 29 ..
Indeed, it dispels bad dreams and destroys the great sins;
it calms great obstacles and brings great peace to men. .. 2.1.28.30 ..
Since by mere remembrance it eradicates all the sins of men,
one should drink that enchanting sacred water with the eight-syllable mantra itself, .. 31 ..
or one may drink the water with names beginning with Keśava,
or else one should drink the auspicious sacred water with the three names, .. 32 ..
or indeed with the eight-syllable mantra of Veṅkaṭeśa.
One should drink that Kaṭāhatīrtha, which bestows worldly enjoyment and liberation. .. 33 ..
The brahmin who drinks that supreme sacred water without a mantra,

2.1.m: [should say,] 'Quickly destroy my great sin committed in other births!' .. 34 ..
Saying this, he should daily drink the sole means to the path of liberation.
A ritual ablution in the Svāmipuṣkariṇī, the darśana of Varāha and the Lord of Śrī, .. 35 ..
and the drinking of the Kaṭāhatīrtha: this triad is rare in the three worlds.
What need of saying much here? It destroys [the sin of] murdering a brahmin and the like. .. 36 ..
Now, the narrative of the brahmin named Keśava.
Formerly, a certain brahmin named Keśava, out of delusion,
killed a learned man with a sword through foolishness, and incurred [the sin of] murdering a brahmin. .. 37 ..
Even he, having drunk the unexcelled water in that great sacred ford,
that great sinner named Keśava was freed from the murder of a brahmin. .. 38 ..
The seers said:

2.1.m: Whose son was the one named Keśava? How did he contract that terrifying
[and] the most terrifying brahmahatyā? You ought to tell us.
The venerable Sūta said:
On the delightful bank of the Tuṅgabhadrā, frequented by gandharvas,
there was a great agrahāra known by the name of Vedāḍhya.
In that charming Vedapura, there were brahmins who had mastered the Vedas,
all devoted to grammar and proficient in the science of astronomy.
They were learned in Mīmāṃsā and logic, and all expounded Vedānta.
They were devoted to the legal treatises and constantly engaged in giving food.
All those eminent people in the agrahāra had sons.
In that Vedāḍhya agrahāra there was one renowned as Padmanābha.
Now begins the sequence of the brahmin Keśava, lustful for a courtesan, contracting brahmahatyā.
His son was named Keśava, who was excluded from all rites.
Abandoning his mother, his father, and even his devoted wife,
ever attached to a courtesan, he entered the house of a harlot.
Having enjoyed that harlot for two days, the brahmin then,

When he was without wealth, he was cast off by the harlot, yet he remained solely intent on union with her.
Stealing much wealth incessantly from here and there,

2.1.m: From a single cup he drank wine together with her.

Padmanābha said:

Hearing that, brahmahatyā said to that Padmanābha:

'This son of yours has fallen; he is excluded from social classes and stages of life.

Now the means of release from brahmahatyā spoken by Bharadvāja to Padmanābha.

By good fortune, O Śaunaka and others of great splendor, the yogi arrived. (66)

2.1.m: meditated for a very long time, and then spoke these words to Padmanābha: (74)
Bharadvāja said:
“O Padmanābha, a most cruel sin was committed by your son.
There can be no expiation of this sin even by ten thousand penances. (75)
Even so, for the pacification of this sin of your son,
I shall declare an expiation; listen, O Padmanābha, O brahmin! (76)
Two hundred yojanas south of the Gaṅgā, O brahmin,
at a measure of five yojanas west of the eastern ocean, (77)
and just one krośa north of the bank of the Suvarṇamukharī,
[there is a mountain] known as Veṅkaṭādri, bowed to by all worlds, (78)
the son of Meru, greatly holy, praised by all the gods,
the great pleasure-mountain of Viṣṇu, brought from the realm of Vaikuṇṭha (79)
by swift Garuḍa to the auspicious bank of the Svarṇamukhī;
it stands worshipped by hosts of gods and hosts of seers. (80)
On that king of mountains, Veṅkaṭa, Nārāyaṇa himself in visible form,
having arrived together with the goddess Lakṣmī, the goddess Bhū, and the goddess Nīlā, (81)
resides as that Veṅkaṭeśa who directly bestows liberation.
To the north of the temple of that Lord of Veṅkaṭa, (82)
there is, O best of brahmins, the Kaṭāhatīrtha, which bestows auspiciousness,
destroys sins such as brahmahatyā, and bestows desired objects. (83)

The seers said:
The greatness of all the sacred fords here has been told by you,
as well as of the rivers, mountains, sacred fields, and lakes.
By command of Brahmā, the Suvarṇamukharī river,
brought to earth by Agastya, has been recounted by you, O sinless one.
Delight has arisen in us to hear its origin and power,
and the multitude of sacred fords connected to it; therefore you ought to tell it to us.

2.1.m: Having bowed to Śambhu, Nandīśa, the six-faced one, and Vyāsa,
the Sūta, requested by the sages, then began to speak.
Śrī Sūta said:
It is well asked by you, O fortunate ones, bringing auspiciousness—
this narrative, which grants the attainment born from hearing sacred tradition.
Listen attentively to the divine tale that destroys impurities;
I shall tell you what Bharadvāja told to Arjuna.
Having obtained Draupadī from the wise Drupada, the sons of Pṛthā,
at the command of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, went to auspicious Hastināpura.
Honored there at that time by Bhīṣma and the son of Ambikā,
they lived together with Duryodhana and the others for five years.
Then the highly renowned Dhṛtarāṣṭra, instructed by Bhīṣma and the rest,
in the presence of all the elders of the lineage and Vāsudeva,
his heart delighted by their service, gave to the sons of Pāṇḍu
half the kingdom, including the excellent city named Khāṇḍavaprastha.
Taking leave of the Kurus headed by Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the sons of Pāṇḍu
went to that city of Khāṇḍavaprastha accompanied by Kṛṣṇa.
Dwelling in that city called Indraprastha, protected by Viśvakarman,
Yudhiṣṭhira, along with his younger brothers, ruled the earth.

In regular order, that Draupadī, with respect,
should stay in the house of each one for one year, according to a mutual agreement.
Whoever should see her while she stays in another's house,
must observe resort to sacred fords for the period of one year.
Having made such a pledge, those sons of King Pāṇḍu,
untiring, passed the time in ordinary worldly affairs.
Then a rural brahmin, standing in the courtyard of the royal palace,
cried out repeatedly: 'My cow has been stolen by thieves!'

There he saw Draupadī and Yudhiṣṭhira seated together;

Yudhiṣṭhira said:
An untrue word that one speaks for the sake of a cow or for a brahmin,
or an improper deed that one performs, is truth; it is right.

how could that take on the nature of wrongdoing? Tell me, O you of noble vows!
In the duty of protecting subjects, through neglecting or punishing thieves,
surely the fruit for a king is that of brahmin-slaughter or of an Aśvamedha.
Even knowing enemies are incurable, a king does not attain fortune
if thieves who cause devastation in his country are left unpunished.

Śrī Sūta said:
Having heard the words of Dharmaputra, with folded hands
Dhanañjaya, ever devoted to righteousness, spoke again:
Arjuna said:
“O king, do not speak thus, violating your own vow,
when you know the essence of righteousness, being the radiant embodiment of righteousness.
A pledge spoken before by oneself who knows what ought and ought not to be done, who is capable—
that vow must never be broken by a man.
That is the resort of the weak: that on the word of kinsmen or teachers

If the noble one should turn [me] back from going to sacred fords out of pity,
who would stop the people who prate of me as one who has broken his vow?
Moreover, my mind is eager with longing for the pilgrimage to sacred fords,
and the command ordained by Nārada has been remembered as duty, O king.
Therefore be gracious, O great king, in this undertaking to go to sacred fords;
for the compact of dependents ought to be respected by lords.”
Saying ‘So be it,’ Arjuna, having obtained permission together with his brothers,
gratified his elder brother with salutations, humble deference, and the like.
Having taken leave of his brothers, Bhīmasena and the rest, as was fitting, the Pāṇḍava,
with rites for auspiciousness performed by worthy brahmins, departed.
Reciters of Purāṇas, astrologers, physicians, brahmins,
hosts of servants, artisans, bards, and panegyrists followed [him].
By order of Yudhiṣṭhira, taking wealth sufficient for enjoyment and charity,
affectionate courtiers and treasury officers accompanied [him].
Now Arjuna’s arrival at Suvarṇamukharī after bathing in the Gaṅgā and other sacred fords:

2.1.m: First reaching the river Bhāgīrathī, that prince
served Gaṅgādvāra, Prayāga, and Kāśī as well.
Viewing the sacred fords of the Jāhnavī along the road bordering its banks,
he reached the southern ocean with its towering billows.
Having beheld the great, highly auspicious Mahānadī, the renowned Puruṣottama,
and Siṃhācala, he attained the fulfillment of his purpose.

2.1.m: Then the son of Kuntī saw the sacred Godāvarī river,
whose majesty rises transcendent by destroying the multitude of all sins.
Having bathed according to rule in its waters, the son of Pāṇḍu
made gladness with diverse gifts of land and gold.

2.1.m: And seeing the river named Malāpahā, he experienced auspicious joy;
then he reached the Kṛṣṇaveṇī, the best of rivers.
He beheld Śrīparvata, the perpetual abode of Śiva,
endowed with four gates and crowded with various assemblies of sacred fords.
Crossing the river Pinākinī, having gone on, he saw Mount Veṅkaṭa,
served by divine seers and the cherished abode of Nārāyaṇa.
Hari, the sole lord of the world, residing on the high peak of this mountain,
the renowned one, he worshipped with devotion for the attainment of good fortune.
Descending from the lofty peak of Mount Veṅkaṭa, he saw the river named Suvarṇamukharī,
frequented by assemblies of perfected beings and sages, brought down by the pot-born sage.

2.1.m: Thus ends the twenty-ninth chapter, named ‘Description of Arjuna’s Departure on Pilgrimage to Sacred Fords’ in the Suvarṇamukharīmāhātmya of the Śrī Veṅkaṭācalamāhātmya, in the second [book], the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Now the description of Suvarṇamukharī:
Sūta said:
And to Pārtha, who had thus arrived after beholding all the sacred fords,
that great river multiplied his delight;
in the bowers on whose banks women rejoice at ease
and perfected beings are attended by winds cooled by showers of spray;
which, as if raising its hands to embrace the Gaṅgā flowing in the sky,
rises with towering billows that touch the clouds;
the grounds of the hermitages on whose banks shine with smoke born of oblations clinging to tree branches
and with garments of bark.
Installed all around by foremost sages and the best of gods,
on both of whose banks shine the divine liṅgas of the Trident-bearer;
resting in their dwelling upon whose sandbanks,
swans, the finest of birds, do not remember their own abode, the Mānasa lake;
who, having allayed the terror of drought by waters issued from the mouths of irrigation channels,
nourishes the crops that are capable of preserving the world;
adorned with ripples like creeping vines, with cakravāka birds as her lofty breasts,
having the expanse of sandbanks as her hips, and whirlpools gleaming as her navel;
with blossoming lotuses as her face, darting pairs of fish as her eyes,
glistening foam as her garment, charming with her gait of swans;
having the cries of waterbirds as her conversation, delighting the eyes,
she who shines as the ocean's beloved, having the form of an extraordinary lovely woman.
On the eastern bank of that river flowing between its bounds, Dhanañjaya
saw a towering mountain named Kālahasti,
which scraped the celestial vault with the sweep of its lofty peaks,
and was adorned with foundation-stones firmly rooted deep below the seven Pātālas.
Now Arjuna's arrival to worship Kālahastīśvara and others on the bank of the Svarṇamukharī.
Having bathed in that great river, on that mountain Arjuna saw the god
worshiped by the gods, known by the name Kālahastīśa.
And having worshipped Mahādeva, the companion of the daughter of the mountain king,
with a mind filled with devotion, he attained the fulfillment of his purpose.
Then, on that great mountain, the sole abode of wonders,
he wandered about, eager to see marvels never seen before.
He beheld siddhas dwelling on the mountain slopes,
accompanied by women, singing the exploits of the god of gods;
enjoyed by celestial women, excited with the intoxication of flower-wine,
he respectfully looked upon Gandharvas seated in bowers;
in secluded places, dedicated to meditation on Śiva,
he saw divine yogins possessed of reverence and joy;
all around, the Pāṇḍava observed tranquil hermitage sites,
their entrance grounds glistening with offerings of wild grains;
fasting, feeding on wind, eating fallen leaves, subsisting on heat,
he beheld peaceful sages whose senses were restrained.
Lakes of lotuses brought joy to his eyes,
scenting the intermediate directions with the fragrance of blooming saugandhika lilies.
Their minds engrossed in hunting, wandering with strung bows,
Now Arjuna's arrival at the hermitage of Bharadvāja on the bank of the Suvarṇamukharī.
he saw Kirātas accompanied by their wives, searching for deer.
Then, wandering in the charming southern quarter of the mountain,
the Kaurava beheld the holy hermitage of Bharadvāja,
with plantains, coconuts, mangoes, jujubes, campakas, and sandaltrees,
takkolas, aśokas, hintālas, palmyras, ketakīs, and pomegranates,
rose apples, kadambas, katakas, khadiras, arjunas, and pāṭalas,
nāgas, punnāgas, saralas, devodārus, and karañjas,
with cloves, luṅgas, lavalīs, priyaṅgus, and tilakas too,
bibhītakas, bilvas, aśvatthas, madhūkas, plakṣas, and kesaras,
areca palms, citrons, oranges, nimba, āmalaka, and kauśika trees,
and adorned with other trees rich in fruits and flowers,
entwined with vāsantī, kunda, jasmine, and other creepers,
with female bees attracted all around by its extraordinary fragrance,
giving shelter to cakravākas, cranes, krauñcas, swans, and kāraṇḍavas,
graced with multitudes of saugandhika lilies, blue lotuses, water lilies, and white lotuses,
endowed with beauty by lakes of sweet and abundant water trickling like nectar,
the sole home of wonders,
thronged with lions, elephants, tigers, hyenas, ruru deer, and antelopes,
and other wild animals acting benevolently toward one another,
surpassing the Caitraratha garden and putting the Nandana grove to shame,
exalted beyond speech and mind, the cause of supreme bliss,
where sweet-voiced parrots reveal to their fledglings
the peerless collection of meanings of the divine Śaiva scriptures.
Where the sky, darkened by the smoke of sacrificial fires,
spreads the illusion of out-of-season clouds to peacocks;
Where elephants, approaching at will, cool the limbs
of lions exhausted from play, with sprays from their trunks—
beholding that hermitage, his mind struck with wonder,
the son of Pāṇḍu praised the power of the ascetics.
Halting all his attendants right there,
Now, the manner of Bharadvāja's service by Arjuna:
he entered that hermitage together with his friends, the eminent brahmins.
Ahead, the son of Kuntī beheld Bharadvāja,
resplendent with the brilliance of flashing fire, surrounded by many foremost sages,
his whole body smeared with ash, his upper garment a deer skin,
radiant like Mount Kailāsa wrapped in a fresh cloud,
shining with hanging matted locks that possessed a golden luster,
like an autumn cloud strewn with motionless lightning-streaks,
as if he were an embodied form assumed by the meanings of Śruti, Smṛti, and the Purāṇas
assembled into one, the auspicious abode of divine knowledge,
constantly served by steadfastness, forbearance, compassion, contentment, and peace,
as if by beloved women devoted to him, possessing unbroken spiritual splendor.
Approaching slowly, Pārtha made a prostration
with all eight limbs touching the ground before the sage’s lotus feet.
Now, the manner of hospitality shown by Bharadvāja to Arjuna:
Raising up the son of Pṛthā who had arrived, the eminent sage,
his heart blossoming with great joy, cheered him with blessings.
And duly honoring that dear guest with the guest-offering and other rites,
he inquired after his health as he sat upon the designated seat.
Having received honor from this sage, the middle Pāṇḍava
brought delight to the mind of the chief of sages with kind words.
Then Bharadvāja remembered the heavenly cow that milks desires;
she prepared an abundant feast of various foods and delicacies.
Having eaten, Pārtha attended upon that treasury of austerity along with his followers,
and spent the rest of the day pleasantly in conversational exchange.
Then, having performed the evening ritual and made offerings to the sacred fire,
he went together with the brahmins and ministers to the sage's huts.
Seated there, congratulated with blessings by the lord of sages,
delighted, he rejoiced in the cool breezes of that river.

Now, the inquiry of Arjuna to Bharadvāja out of a desire to hear the majesty of Suvarṇamukharī:
The glorious Sūta said:
Having performed his evening rites, blazing with the brilliance of fire,
the bull of the Bharatas bowed down to the comfortably seated lord of sages.
Delighted by the flow of nectar-like, cool fragrance belonging to it,
he spoke these profound and humble words:
Arjuna said:
O eminent sage, in this world I alone am truly fortunate,
since I am properly honored by you no differently than a son.
My mind, filled with curiosity aroused by your hospitality,
seems to hasten me to drink the divine nectar of your words.
From what mountain was this great river born? By whom was she brought?
What religious merit is obtained there through ritual ablutions, gifts, and the like?

Now begins the narrative of the marriage of Śaṃkara, recounted by Bharadvāja:
Formerly, the goddess Dākṣāyaṇī, having been insulted by her father,
abandoned that body and became the daughter of the Snow Mountain.
Approached and entreated by the seven seers, the Mountain,
prepared to give his daughter in marriage to Mṛtyuṃjaya.
He whose emblem is the bull, the Lord of the universe, in order to marry Sarvamaṅgalā,
arrived at Himavat's dwelling named Oṣadhiprastha.
By his command, all immobile and mobile beings assembled,
in order to rejoice at the wedding of the Lord of creatures.
Crushed by their immense weight, the earth in the northern region
sank so deep that it reached down to Pātāla.

In this manner, this divine river, by providing for bathing, drinking, and the like,

By command of the lotus-born [Brahmā], the river flowing from the sky,
under the name of Suvarṇamukharī, purifies those who seek refuge in her alone.
Traversing in succession many great mountains, expanses of forest, and many regions, this best of rivers,
attended by great rivers born of mountains,
carrying waters that bestow singular freedom from disease upon those stricken with sickness and exceedingly distressed,
which remove the intense inner and outer heat and cause delight,
and with a multitude of spray risen from the swift and mighty blows of the trunks of lordly elephants sportive in their play,
as if joyfully presenting an offering of flowers to the maker of the day [the sun],
which are clear against their source, fragrant with the perfume of blue water-lilies, lotuses, and white water-lilies that scent the quarters of the sky,
the sole abodes of good fortune for bees;
reddened by the red vermilion dust from the partings of the hair of celestial nymphs eager for playful plunges,
perfumed with the fragrance of pārijāta blossoms fallen from their masses of hair;
she, bearing waters filled with auspiciousness, sweet, free of mud, exceedingly clear,
resembling nectar, born of the son of the lord of the gods [Indra], and destroying sins,
having taken her birth from Mount Agastya, brought to earth by the pot-born sage [Agastya],
resplendent with hosts of celebrated sacred fords, reached the southern ocean.

Embracing her with wave-hands and honouring her as she arrived,
the lord of rivers showed affection with loud-resounding speeches.

Having thus united the river with the ocean,
