one overcomes having bathed in the water of the Suvarṇamukharī.
Giving a piece of land measured by a cow's foot on the bank of the Suvarṇamukharī,
one obtains whatever fruit is gained from giving the entire earth.
Having given a cow along with cloth and ornaments on the bank of the Suvarṇamukharī
to a brahmin according to the rule, one goes to the eternal Brahman.
On auspicious occasions, all kinds of gifts should be made
on the bank of the Suvarṇamukharī, to attain fruit in this world and the next. // 53
Recitation, oblation, austerity, gift, rites for the ancestors, worship of the gods—
whatever is performed on the bank of the Suvarṇamukharī becomes a hundredfold. // 54
I shall tell you another excellent vow that should be observed
on the bank of the Suvarṇamukharī every year by those who desire happiness. // 55
When, having disappeared with the sun's rays in the rainy season,
the glorious sage, the son of Mitra and Varuṇa, rises, // 56
those who, self-controlled, take a ritual ablution in her on that day

2.1.s: taiḥ kalpaṃ ca surāvāse sthīyate kurunandana .. 57 ..
2.1.d: तैः कल्पं च सुरावासे स्थीयते कुरुनन्दन .. 57 ..
2.1.m: dwell in the abode of the gods for an eon, O son of Kuru. // 57
Those who then give an image of Agastya made of gold

2.1.s: vidhinā dadate pārtha te yāṃti brahma śāśvatam .. 58 ..
2.1.d: विधिना ददते पार्थ ते यांति ब्रह्म शाश्वतम् .. 58 ..
2.1.m: according to rule, O son of Pṛthā, go to the eternal Brahman. // 58
Arjuna said:
By what rule should this vow be performed, O great sage?
Tell all that to me, a noble one who is eager to know. // 59
Now the procedure for giving the image of Agastya.
Bharadvāja said:
Having learned the day of Agastya's rising, with a controlled mind
one should have an image of that great sage fashioned from gold according to one's means: // 2.1.33.60
possessing a luster brilliant as gold, charming with bound matted locks,
holding a rosary and a water pot in his two lotus-like hands, // 61
wearing soft bark-cloth, with a deer-skin upper garment,
gentle, lovely with marks of sacred ash, adorned with rudrākṣa beads. // 62
Having thus fashioned that image, having bathed, with a controlled mind,
having adorned the preceptor with fragrant pastes, flowers, and the like according to rule, // 63
one should worship that image placed upon an āḍhaka measure
of rice from winter crops, provided with two garments: // 64
"O restrainer of the Vindhya mountain, expert in swallowing the ocean in a sip,
greatly illuminated by the radiance of all the gods beginning with Brahmā, // 65
O Agastya born from a jar, bowed to by gods and asuras,
may the Lord obtain great delight from this gift of mine." // 66
Having uttered this mantra, having given [it] preceded by pouring water, along with a fee,

2.1.s: dattvā vimuktaḥ pāpebhyo yāti brahma sanātanam .. 67 ..
2.1.d: दत्त्वा विमुक्तः पापेभ्यो याति ब्रह्म सनातनम् .. 67 ..
2.1.m: freed from sins, one goes to the eternal Brahman. // 67
From the floods of great sins and minor sins committed in other births
as well as those committed in this birth, one is surely liberated; there is no doubt about this. // 68
All the gods headed by Brahmā, the great seers headed by Sanaka,

2.1.s: carācarāṇi bhūtāni prītiṃ yāṃti na saṃśayaḥ .. 69 ..
2.1.d: चराचराणि भूतानि प्रीतिं यांति न संशयः .. 69 ..
2.1.m: and the moving and unmoving beings attain delight; there is no doubt. // 69
Having performed this holy vow, and for the satisfaction of the good sage Agastya,
one should feed brahmins according to one's ability, along with a fee. // 2.1.33.70
And if unable to perform that rite, one should, filled with devotion,
please the brahmins according to one's capacity by gifting gold, grain, and the like. // 71
One should not let that lunar day pass in vain; one should observe it with effort;
a person must perform even some small sacred act. // 72
The ripened fruit of the austerity of the great sage Agastya
is the river Suvarṇamukharī, worthy of being praised by gods and asuras. // 73
Thus the origin and power of the great river
have been fully told to you. Now declare what you wish to hear further.

2.1.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe veṃkaṭācalamāhātmye suvarṇamukharīprabhāvapraśaṃsānāma trayastriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 33 ..
2.1.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे वेंकटाचलमाहात्म्ये सुवर्णमुखरीप्रभावप्रशंसानाम त्रयस्त्रिंशोऽध्यायः .. 33 ..
2.1.m: Thus ends the thirty-third chapter, named "Praise of the Power of the Suvarṇamukharī", in the Venkaṭācalamāhātmya in the second section, the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. // 33
Now the power of the Agastyatīrtha and of Agastyeśvara.
Arjuna said:
Even though drinking the nectar of your speech again and again with the folded cups of my ears,

2.1.s: mano nopaiti me tṛptiṃ bhūyaḥ śravaṇakāṅkṣayā .. 1 ..
2.1.d: मनो नोपैति मे तृप्तिं भूयः श्रवणकाङ्क्षया .. 1 ..
2.1.m: my mind does not attain satisfaction, through longing to hear further. // 1
May my repeated desire to listen to your words
not cause mental distress to you whose nature is filled with compassion. // 2
Now I wish to hear, O great sage: in this river,
which sacred fords are efficacious for destroying sin? // 3

2.1.s: kāḥ kāḥ puṇyataraṃgiṇyaḥ saṅgatā anayā mune ..
2.1.d: काः काः पुण्यतरंगिण्यः सङ्गता अनया मुने ..
2.1.m: Which holy rivers are joined with her, O sage?
Where, having cut down their sins through ritual ablution, do people have no fear of Yama? // 4
And what holy abodes of the gods, beginning with Hara and Acyuta,
and whatever holy places there are, stand on both of her banks? // 5
The fruit that is attained by men in those sacred fields,
Through auspicious rites such as ritual ablution and gifts performed according to the rules,
All this, along with the narrative, has been understood, O best of the knowers of the Veda.
Great delight has arisen in me; explain it to me in full detail and in due order.
Bharadvāja said:
What has been asked by you, O Pārtha, is told in full detail and in due order,
The majesty of the multitude of sacred fords of this [river], beginning from Agastya-tīrtha, the foremost of sacred fords.
By the great-souled Agastya, who is the embodiment of unbroken knowledge, / who desires the welfare of all worlds,
And who is worthy of honor by gods and demons—
When it first descended to the earth from that mountain,
Where, having bathed in the great river, one attains the fulfillment of one's purpose,
That is declared in the three worlds to be the purifying Agastya-tīrtha;
By ritual ablution there, purification will occur even for perpetrators of great sins.
Casting off the heap of great sins / committed throughout many births,

2.1.s: nira divi modante tatra snānaratā janāḥ .. 12 ..
2.1.d: निर दिवि मोदन्ते तत्र स्नानरता जनाः .. 12 ..
2.1.m: People devoted to ritual ablution there rejoice in heaven.

2.1.s: ye tatra tīrthe yatinaḥ kṛtasnānā yatendriyāḥ ..
2.1.d: ये तत्र तीर्थे यतिनः कृतस्नाना यतेन्द्रियाः ..
2.1.m: Those self-restrained ascetics who, having performed ritual ablution in that sacred ford,
Bestow great gifts such as cows, land, sesame seeds, and gold,
Attain entirely, O Arjuna, a hundredfold the fruit of the gifts
Performed by focused persons at the Gate of the Gaṅgā.
Here resides the Lord Īśa, renowned by the name Agastyeśa,
Installed by the sage Agastya, who causes joy to the world.

2.1.s: snātvā tasyāṃ mahānadyāṃ talliṃgaṃ pūjayanti ye ..
2.1.d: स्नात्वा तस्यां महानद्यां तल्लिंगं पूजयन्ति ये ..
2.1.m: Those who, having bathed in that great river, worship that liṅga,
They obtain the fruit of ten horse-sacrifices.
Now, the determination of the time for ritual ablution in the Suvarṇamukharī:
When the sun, leaving the sign of Sagittarius,
Enters Capricorn, that meritorious northern course is proclaimed.

2.1.s: tasmindine ye niyatā nadyāṃ snātvā samāhitāḥ ..
2.1.d: तस्मिन्दिने ये नियता नद्यां स्नात्वा समाहिताः ..
2.1.m: On that day, those restrained and focused persons who, having bathed in the river,
Behold Pārvatī's lord, Agastyeśa, worshipped by the gods,
Having attained the fruit of a thousand Agniṣṭoma sacrifices and a hundred Vājapeya sacrifices,
Rejoice in heaven, worshipped by hosts of gods.
At the time of the sun's entry into Capricorn, by men desiring auspiciousness
The darśana of Agastyeśa must certainly be performed.
Now, the māhātmya of the Deva, Ṛṣi, and Pitṛ sacred fords:
To the northeast of that sacred ford, at a distance of one krośa, O Arjuna,
There is a triad of sacred fords, known by the names of Devas, Ṛṣis, and Pitṛs.
The gods, seers, and ancestors, worshipped there by that sage,
With joyful minds granted all desired wishes.
Then it was declared in his presence by the gods, seers, and ancestors:
“This triad of sacred fords, in due order, shall be praiseworthy by our names.”
Those who, having bathed in that triad of sacred fords and offered tarpaṇa rites,
Are completely freed from the three debts, go to imperishable heaven.
Now, the description of the confluence of the Veṇā and the Suvarṇamukharī:
Then, on the ground to the northeast, at a distance of two yojanas,
The great river named Veṇā reached the Suvarṇamukharī;
Trees on its banks felled by the forceful impact of its lofty current,
The forest inundated by torrents of water surging from water-channels,
Crowded with flocks of ruddy geese playing on the high slopes of its sandbanks,
Resounding with the playful hum of swarms of bees eager for the fragrance of lotuses,
Having passed beyond many lofty mountains,
Beautiful with abundant waters, it joined the Suvarṇamukharī.
Those who perform ritual ablution according to the rules at the confluence of the two rivers
Shall attain the complete fruit of ten horse-sacrifices.
Joined with the Veṇā, the holy river Suvarṇamukharī,
Flowing northward, proceeded along an impassable mountain path.
Passing along an uneven path through the midst of the mountains,
That river shone over an extent of four yojanas.
To the east of that place, in a region of one and a half yojanas,
On the charming north bank of the great river that flows to the east,
There is the famed liṅga of the foe of Tripura named Agastyeśvara,
The remembrance of which dispels all sins for gods and mortals.

2.1.s: tatra snātvā mahānadyāṃ ye narā niyatendriyāḥ ..
2.1.d: तत्र स्नात्वा महानद्यां ये नरा नियतेन्द्रियाः ..
2.1.m: Those men who, having bathed there in the great river with senses controlled,
behold the Lord of Pārvatī installed by Agastya,
casting off the accumulation of sin acquired across many previous births,
rejoice in the abode of the gods for imperishable time. // 35
Then turning northward, the Suvarṇamukharī flowed
half a yojana across this region, accompanied by an assemblage of sacred fords. // 36
Now, the confluence of the Suvarṇamukharī and the river named Vyāghrapadā.
In that region, delightful with hintāla, tāla, and sāla trees,
the Suvarṇamukharī and the river named Vyāghrapadā met,
skillful in warding off manifold sins that are hard to avert, // 37-38
adorned with dense groves of reed-thickets along its banks,
rich with the playful plunge of the wives of Siddhas and Gandharvas,
shining with flowers offered as oblations by the daughters of ascetics, // 39
resounding with the clamor of flocks of swans, karaṇḍavas, and krauñcas,
flowing eastward, having arrived by a path running between mountains. // 40
The best among men who perform a ritual ablution there at the confluence of the two rivers
obtain the full fruit of ten horse-sacrifices. // 41
Now, the description of Śaṅkhatīrtha.
There on the bank of the river named Vyāghrapadā, which removes the impurities of the world,
shines the faultless Śaṅkhatīrtha, destroyer of all sins, // 42
the constant dwelling-place of brahmin-seers, visited by gods and Gandharvas,
bestowing boundless joy through sighting, bathing, drinking, and the like. // 43
There abides the divine Lord named Śaṅkheśa, O Phālguna,
installed in the form of a liṅga by the eminent sage named Śaṅkha. // 44

2.1.s: ye tatra tīrthe susnātāḥ paśyanti vṛṣavāhanam ..
2.1.d: ये तत्र तीर्थे सुस्नाताः पश्यन्ति वृषवाहनम् ..
2.1.m: Those who, having bathed well in that sacred ford, behold the One whose mount is a bull,
attain the merit born of ten horse-sacrifices and go to the abode of the gods. // 45

2.1.s: yuktā tayā vyāghrapadābhidhānayā gatvā tato yojanasaṃmitāṃ bhuvam ..
2.1.d: युक्ता तया व्याघ्रपदाभिधानया गत्वा ततो योजनसंमितां भुवम् ..
2.1.m: Joined with that [river] called Vyāghrapadā, having gone thence across an area measured at a yojana,
resorted to by eminent sages, with auspicious, clear waters, she went near Mount Vṛṣabhācala. // 46

2.1.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīveṃkaṭācalamāhātmye'gastyatīrthādivividhatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma catustriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 34 ..
2.1.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीवेंकटाचलमाहात्म्येऽगस्त्यतीर्थादिविविधतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम चतुस्त्रिंशोऽध्यायः .. 34 ..
2.1.m: Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter, named 'Description of the māhātmya of Agastyatīrtha and various sacred fords,' in the Śrīveṅkaṭācalamāhātmya, in the second section, the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, of the glorious Skandamahāpurāṇa comprising eighty-one thousand verses. // 34
Now, the confluence of the Suvarṇamukharī and the Kalyā river.
Bharadvāja said:
There the auspicious Suvarṇamukharī was joined by
the holy river named Kalyā, as the Kālindī [is joined] by the Jāhnavī. // 1
Arising from Mount Vṛṣabhācala, adorned with sovereign sacred fords,
the Kalyā is the best of rivers, destroying hosts of taints, // 2
with both banks adorned with clusters of various trees and creepers,
a comfortable dwelling for hosts of sages, abundant in holy hermitages, // 3
its banks shining with kuśa grass and unbroken grains glistening from water-oblations given by the twice-born,
muddy from washing away the musk-paste on the breasts of apsarases, // 4
made fragrant by the rut-water trickling from elephants' temples,
surrounded by hundreds of sacrificial posts set up for rites by brahmins and kings, // 5
gratifying all men with its flood of clear water.
Even alone, one of the two great rivers is fully capable of destroying sin; // 6

2.1.s: tayoḥ saṃgatayoḥ stotuṃ mahimānaṃ ka īśate ..
2.1.d: तयोः संगतयोः स्तोतुं महिमानं क ईशते ..
2.1.m: who is able to extol their greatness when they are conjoined?
Where, in the midst of the river, stands the stone known as the Brahmaśilā, // 7
and, by Agastya's austerity, Gayā later manifests her presence.
Those who have bathed there in the holy water of the two rivers, O best of Kurus, // 8
obtain the fruit of a hundred pauṇḍarīka sacrifices;
sins such as the killing of a brahmin are completely destroyed // 9
for those purified by ablution there at the confluence of the two rivers,
purifying like the Kṛṣṇaveṇī joined with the Bhavanāśinī. // 10
Now, the description of glorious Mount Veṅkaṭācala situated on the bank of the Suvarṇamukharī.
The Suvarṇamukharī shone, joined then with the Kalyā. // 11
Now, half a yojana to the north of the great river shines
the renowned Mount Veṅkaṭācala, having an elevation of a yojana. // 12
This best of mountains is the refuge of all sacred fords:
Añjanā, Ananta, Vṛṣabha, Nīla, Kesarin, and Potrin— // 13
these are the groves of the mountain, as are Nārāyaṇa and Veṅkaṭa.
Because it was previously claimed by the Enemy of Madhu in the form of a boar, // 14
this mountain is celebrated by noble people as Varāhakṣetra.
On the bank of the Suvarṇamukharī, on the celebrated Veṅkaṭācala,
Acyuta dwells eternally, accompanied by the daughter of the king of the ocean.
While he dwells on that mountain together with Śrī as the Lord of Veṅkaṭa,
Siddhas, gandharvas, sages, humans, and dānavas revere him.
For the devotees whose minds are fixed upon that Highest Person,
wishes are swiftly fulfilled, O Arjuna, and misfortunes are destroyed.
Those who remember the Lord of the World residing on Mount Veṅkaṭa,
with their faults cast aside, reach the eternal, imperishable state.
Arjuna said:
On Mount Veṅkaṭa, which is exceedingly sacred and bowed to by gods and asuras,
how did the divine Lord, the husband of Kamalā, manifest himself?
Or to which virtuous person there, being pleased, did he reveal his wondrous form,
which grants the fruits of worldly enjoyment and liberation?
The greatness of Viṣṇu, the primordial god of gods, O great sage,
I wish to hear in truth; tell it to me in detail.
Now begins the description of the majesty of the Lord residing on the holy Veṅkaṭācala.
Bharadvāja said:
Listen attentively to the greatness of the Lord of Veṅkaṭa;
it cannot be narrated in full even by Brahmā.
Blessed are you, for your mind has become devoted to hearing
the māhātmya of the god of gods, the enemy of Madhu, O tamer of foes, dear friend.
I have acquired merit, O son of Pṛthā, because the purifying deeds
of Hari, the lord of all beings, will now be praised by me.
Formerly, on the bank of the Bhāgīrathī, to the great-souled Janaka,
who was engaged in the consecration for a sacrifice and possessed of pure knowledge,
a tale was told by Vāmadeva that destroys sins;
I shall narrate that purifying tale to you, O son of Pṛthā, celebrating Viṣṇu.
Nārāyaṇa is the first Lord of all beings whatsoever,
composed of the universe, creator of the universe, the taintless nature of consciousness.
The Lord has a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, and a thousand feet,
by whose light this universe, with the moving and unmoving, shines forth.
Splendor higher than he, austerity higher than he,
knowledge higher than he, or yoga higher than he does not exist.

2.1.s: vidyā tasmādapi parā nāsti pārtha nararṣabha ..
2.1.d: विद्या तस्मादपि परा नास्ति पार्थ नरर्षभ ..
2.1.m: Nor is there any wisdom higher than he, O son of Pṛthā, bull among men.

2.1.s: sarveṣvapi ca bhūteṣu sadā sannihitaḥ prabhuḥ .. 31 ..
2.1.d: सर्वेष्वपि च भूतेषु सदा सन्निहितः प्रभुः .. 31 ..
2.1.m: The Lord is always present in all beings,
and all beings abide comfortably within him alone.

2.1.s: sa eva yajño yajvā ca sādhanaṃ sruksruvādikam .. 32 ..
2.1.d: स एव यज्ञो यज्वा च साधनं स्रुक्स्रुवादिकम् .. 32 ..
2.1.m: He alone is the sacrifice, the sacrificer, and the implements such as the sruc and sruva spoons;
he is the fruit, the giver of the fruit, and likewise the destination to be reached through it.
When the fire is brought forth, with the sprinkled sacrificial animal they offer oblations;

2.1.s: ye taṃ prayāṃti te yāṃti gatiṃ tatpratipāditām .. 33 ..
2.1.d: ये तं प्रयांति ते यांति गतिं तत्प्रतिपादिताम् .. 33 ..
2.1.m: those who approach him go to the state established by him.
Having made the bond of action the sacrificial animal, when the fire of knowledge is kindled,
those who offer oblations directed to him share in union with him.

2.1.s: hariḥ sadāśivo brahmā mahendraḥ paramaḥ svarāṭ ..
2.1.d: हरिः सदाशिवो ब्रह्मा महेन्द्रः परमः स्वराट् ..
2.1.m: Hari, Sadāśiva, Brahmā, Mahendra, the Supreme, the Sovereign—
these are declared to be synonymous terms for that Lord of All.
He who with collected mind meditates upon this māhātmya

2.1.s: nārāyaṇasya māhātmyaṃ sa na yāti punarbhavam .. 36 ..
2.1.d: नारायणस्य माहात्म्यं स न याति पुनर्भवम् .. 36 ..
2.1.m: of the Supreme Self, Nārāyaṇa, does not undergo rebirth.
Consisting of consciousness and bliss, the witness, free from gunas, devoid of limiting conditions,
though eternal, he assumes this or that state at will.

2.1.s: pavitrāṇāṃ pavitraṃ yo hyagatīnāṃ parā gatiḥ ..
2.1.d: पवित्राणां पवित्रं यो ह्यगतीनां परा गतिः ..
2.1.m: He who is the purest of the pure and the supreme refuge of the refugeless,

2.1.s: daivataṃ devatānāṃ ca śreyasāṃ śreya uttamam .. 38 ..
2.1.d: दैवतं देवतानां च श्रेयसां श्रेय उत्तमम् .. 38 ..
2.1.m: the deity of deities, and the highest good among good things,

2.1.s: bodhyānāṃ bodhya eko'sau dhyeyānāṃ dhyeya uttamaḥ ..
2.1.d: बोध्यानां बोध्य एकोऽसौ ध्येयानां ध्येय उत्तमः ..
2.1.m: he alone is the one to be known among things to be known, the highest to be meditated upon among things to be meditated upon,
the supreme humility endowed with wisdom among humilities,

2.1.s: tejasāṃ janakaṃ tejaḥ prakṛṣṭaṃ tapasāṃ tapaḥ ..
2.1.d: तेजसां जनकं तेजः प्रकृष्टं तपसां तपः ..
2.1.m: the splendor that generates splendors, the foremost austerity of austerities,
the support of all beings, without beginning or end, is Janārdana.
Even Brahmā and the others are bewildered in understanding his true nature;

2.1.s: ajo gṛhṇāti jananaṃ sarvātmā hanti vidviṣaḥ .. 41 ..
2.1.d: अजो गृह्णाति जननं सर्वात्मा हन्ति विद्विषः .. 41 ..
2.1.m: unborn, he assumes birth; being the Self of all, he slays enemies;
though independent, he behaves as dependent upon his devotees.

The praṇava (Om) is praised, then his luminous heart,

Whoever constantly recites this king of mantras with composed mind
shall become a vessel of perfections through the grace of Viṣṇu.

Which removes distress, brings prosperity, and bestows enjoyment and liberation—
how Mādhava created beings at the very beginning of the kalpa,

2.1.m: the constant protector of the waters, of all medicinal plants, and of brahmins.
From his two eyes arose the sun, the illuminator of the universe,
the maker of cold, heat, and rain, the cause of time, and the treasury of splendours.
From his life-breaths was born the wind, the life-breath of the world,
possessing great strength, the upholder of planets, constellations, the celestial Gaṅgā, and aerial chariots.
From the navel region of the Great-Souled One the atmosphere arose;
from his head was the sky, the cause of the appearance of living beings.
From his two lotus feet arose the earth, the shelter of the multitude of beings;
from the two ears of the Supreme Self all the cardinal directions went forth.
So too, the worlds beginning with Bhūr and Bhuvas arose from his thought,
as well as the worlds beginning with Rasātala, and the hosts of yakṣas, rākṣasas, and others.
From his mouth, arms, thighs, and feet he brought forth in order
the brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras, O bearer of the Kuru lineage.
The Vedic metres, sacrifice, horses, cattle, sheep, and goats
obtained their origin of unfathomable source from him.
By the intention of that god of gods, all that is immobile and mobile,
the whole host of beings, came to be, as well as time—past, future, and present.
Assuming the form of the submarine fire, he drinks the water of the oceans;
at the end of a kalpa, he emits all that is contained within himself.
Assuming the forms of the sun and moon, he sets in motion the livelihood of living beings,
both by dispelling darkness and by setting in motion the duties of time.
Placing the worlds inside his belly at the close of a kalpa,
he rests on a banyan leaf upon the great ocean, having sportively assumed the form of an infant.
And then, upon the bed of coils of the mighty king of serpents, fit for his comfort,
he enters into yogic sleep, accompanied by her whose abode is the lotus.
From the lotus born of the lake of his navel,
the lord of all worlds generated the four-faced Creator.
For this is the sport of Mukunda, who acts by the yoga of his own will;

Now follows the manner of the lifting of the earth by the Boar.
Bharadvāja said:
Formerly, at the end of the Creator's night, awakened, the slayer of Madhu
carefully considered in his intellect the renewed activity of living beings.
"Except for the earth, none others are capable
of bearing the multitude of beings"—such reasoning arose in his heart.
By deep meditation he saw the earth abiding in Pātāla,
shaken by extreme fear and surrounded by vast waters.
He then assumed a form suited for lifting up the earth:
having the preparatory rites as his lips, fire as his tongue, and the roaring of the praṇava;
having the four Vedas as his legs, and expiations adorning his hooves;
having the prāgvaṃśa hall as his body, accompanied by a row of shining darbha grass as his hair;
endowed with the pravargya ceremony as his whorls, possessing the southern fire as his belly;
having the sacrificial ladle as his snout, with the joints of his limbs fully divided by all [sacrificial elements];
having the collection of divine hymns as his mane, and the Supreme Brahman as his head;
endowed with the speed of oblations to gods and ancestors, with pure sacrificial beasts as his knees;
endowed with the strength of the mantras and paths of metres such as uktā and atyuktā;
assuming the divine boar form, consisting of all sacrifices,
he entered into the waters of the ocean to search for the earth.
Forcibly dispelling with the mass of gleaming radiance arising from his tusk-crescent moon
the darkness that had swelled at the time of the end of the kalpa,
making the cave of the cosmic egg resound constantly with roars
surpassing the thunder of clouds, through his deep grunting sounds,
his body lacerated by the movements of the tips of his hooves,
tossing about here and there the sovereign of the serpents,
with the violent winds of his breath making visible the bottomless interior
of the lord of rivers down to Pātāla,
with his exceedingly long vessel sinking and emerging from the ocean,
agitating the waters, he then went within.
Seeing the earth situated beneath the base of the seven Pātālas in the water,
trembling and overcome with fear, his heart was delighted.
Placing her upon the tip of his tusk, he emerged from the ocean,
being praised by the sages residing in Janaloka.
As the god affectionately carried the earth for a moment,
the ocean below became an auspicious bridal ornament.
At the moment of her lifting up by him who had the boar's body, O Arjuna,
the ocean, with its deep roar, became an auspicious drum;
joined by showers of spray cast up by rolling waves,
the heap of pearls took on the appearance of auspicious consecrated rice grains.

2.1.m: Held up by that god and flooded with water, she shone
as though her body were moistened by sweat produced by intense passion.
Having thus lifted the earth from the base of Pātāla,
the Lord firmly established it amid the waters of the ocean.
When the earth was lifted up by him, the water that filled the space between earth and sky
then became bounded by the limits set by him.
Having thus established the earth, for the sake of securing her support
he stationed the directional elephants, the serpent king, and the tortoise.
And as the support for all of them as well, respectfully

2.1.s: tato dharāṃ samuddhṛtya sthitaṃ kiṭitanuṃ harim .. 24 ..
2.1.d: ततो धरां समुद्धृत्य स्थितं किटितनुं हरिम् .. 24 ..
2.1.m: Then, to Hari standing in the boar form after lifting up the earth,
Sanaka and the others residing in Janaloka offered praise.
Then, having worshipped the Supreme Person in the form of the boar,
by his command Brahmā fashioned the world as before.
Arjuna said:
"How does this earth remain submerged in the water at the end of the kalpa?
Beneath the seven worlds of Pātāla, what is its support, O great sage?
How long is this period of a kalpa, and what is its course?"
Now, the description of the advent of the white boar preceded by the description of the events of the kalpa.
"Explain all this in detail to me, O brahmin sage!"
Bharadvāja said:
"From sixty vināḍikās there is one nāḍikā. A day consists
of sixty of them. Thirty days make a month consisting of two fortnights.
Two months are called a season; from six of them there is a year,
having the form of two solstices, embracing cold, rain, and heat.
For the gods and the asuras, this [year] is one day and night, by inversion:
the sun's northern course and southern course are [their day and night] respectively.
By four million, three hundred and twenty thousand human years,
a Mahāyuga is formed, O son of Pṛthā, consisting of the Kṛta and the other [yugas].
The period of seventy-one yugas is an interval of a Manu (manvantara).
Hear of the Manus born in this [kalpa] called the Śvetavarāha kalpa.
The first is Svāyambhuva; after him, the Manu Svārociṣa;
then Uttama, the one called Tāmasa, Raivata, and the one named Cākṣuṣa.
These six past Manus were accompanied by their Indras, gods, and ascetics.
The seventh Manu, Vaivasvata, is current now, O Arjuna.
The hosts of gods at his time are the Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, and others.
Having performed a hundred horse sacrifices, the radiant [Purandara] attained the status of Indra.
Viśvāmitra, myself, Atri, Jamadagni, Kaśyapa,
Vasiṣṭha, and Gautama—these indeed are the seven seers, O Arjuna.
The sons of the Manu, heroic and mighty, led by Ikṣvāku,
ruled the earth, ever devoted to righteousness.
The five sons of Sūrya, Dakṣa, Brahmā, Dharma, and Rudra,
beginning with Sāvarṇi, Raucya, and Bhauma, will be the future seven Manus.
Fourteen Manus exist in a single day of the Creator.
That is known as a kalpa; at its end, a night of equal duration occurs. Listen:
At the close of Brahmā's day, O son of Pāṇḍu,
a dreadful drought lasting a hundred years occurs on earth.
During that drought, when the earth is depleted of moisture, O Dhanañjaya,
the four kinds of living beings meet complete destruction.
Then, having rays shaped like blazing flames, the sun,
with beams like fire, vomits showers of sparks.
With its villages, cities, mountains, trees, and forests destroyed,
the earth resembles the back of a tortoise, looking like a red-hot lump of iron.
Then, vast clouds arise from the limbs of the Creator,
covering the sky, resounding with thunder.
White, yellow, crimson, dark, and of diverse colors, terrifying,
taking on various shapes such as mountains, elephants, palaces, and trees,
they unleash a torrential downpour for a period of a hundred years.
By that water, the great fire born from the sun is extinguished.
And the great clouds fiercely rain for yet another hundred years.
Swollen with that water, overflowing their shores, the oceans become agitated.
That water discharged by the clouds of the cosmic dissolution encompasses the worlds.
A great darkness envelops the Bhūrloka, Bhuvarloka, Svarloka, and Maharloka.
Then, submerged in water, sunk down to the base of Pātāla,
the earth remains somehow undestroyed, supported by the power of Brahmā.
Then, O Arjuna, the wind born from the breath of Brahmā
disperses all those great clouds that arose at the end of the kalpa.
Thus intensified, the wind blows continuously for a period of a hundred years,
arisen with an irresistible velocity.
Escaping that fierce wind, upon the navel-lotus of Hari,
the lotus-born [Brahmā] enters yogic sleep upon that water.
While that sovereign of the world is engaged in yogic sleep,
the night lasts for as long as the duration of the day, O son of Pṛthā.
When the night has passed, awakened once again with vigor,
he creates all creatures as before, by the command of Hari.
Kalpa after kalpa, Hari protects the universe through appropriate forms.
In this kalpa, he assumed the white form of the sacrificial boar.
Roaming upon the surface of the earth in the body of a boar, the god
resorted to Mount Veṅkaṭa, his own previously designated dwelling.
Wandering for a long time on the bank of the Svāmipuṣkariṇī lake, Adhokṣaja
saw Brahmā, endowed with supreme devotion.
Having worshipped him, Brahmā prayed to that source of all beings:
"O Lord, assume your ancient, divine body."
Accepting his entreaty, he abandoned that boar form
and assumed his own cosmic body, worthy of exclusive worship.
Even after putting forth powerful exertion, [though he] stayed thus on that mountain,

Now begins the account of the king named Śaṅkha.
Bhāradvāja said:
Listen, O son of Pṛthā! I will narrate a wonderful story
of how that Blessed Lord came to manifestation on this mountain. // 1
There was a king named Śruta, born in the lineage of the Haihayas,

2.1.s: yaḥ prajāḥ svā iva ciraṃ śaśāsa dharaṇīṃ śubhām .. 2 ..
2.1.d: यः प्रजाः स्वा इव चिरं शशास धरणीं शुभाम् .. 2 ..

2.1.d: तस्य पुत्रो गुणनिधिः शंखो नाम महीपतिः ..
2.1.m: His son, a treasury of virtues, was a king named Śaṅkha,
learned in all sacred sciences, who protected the earth. // 3
Toward Viṣṇu, the Lord of the world, whose eyes are wide like lotuses,
he had unwavering devotion, having abandoned reliance on any other. // 4
The God of gods, the Lord of the world, the infinite Supreme Person,
whose majesty is wondrous, he constantly meditated upon with firm resolve. // 5

2.1.s: cakre vratāni dānāni puṇyāni vividhāni ca ..
2.1.d: चक्रे व्रतानि दानानि पुण्यानि विविधानि च ..
2.1.m: He performed various observances, gifts, and meritorious acts,
constantly for the pleasure of the Foe of Madhu, who is known through the Vedas. // 6
Directly intended for him alone, he performed sacrifices such as the horse-sacrifice,
pleasing all the brahmins through the grant of the prescribed priestly gifts. // 7
Unflagging, he performed all kinds of religious and philanthropic rites,
with his heart constantly fixed on Keśava, who is affectionate to his devotees. // 8
He incessantly remembers Govinda, mutters [the names of] the imperishable Acyuta,
worships the lotus-eyed one, and praises the Wielder of the Śārṅga bow. // 9
The king constantly listens to the sacred tales of Viṣṇu,
narrated by reciters of the Purāṇas, which ferry [beings] across the ocean of worldly existence. // 10
He worshiped the brahmins solely for the pleasure of Hari.
Though thus engaged with all his being, unwearied, the lord of the earth
did not see the independent Supreme Person of eternal sovereignty. // 11
Not having obtained the darśana of Viṣṇu, whose essence comprises all sacrifices,
his heart was overwhelmed with sorrow, and he fell into intense anxiety. // 12–13
Śaṅkha said:
Much past misdeed must have been done by me
over thousands of births, since the darśana of Hṛṣīkeśa has not been attained! // 14
For the darśana of Viṣṇu, the Slayer of Madhu, is the unbroken fruit
of darkness-dispelling merits accumulated through many previous lives. // 15
How indeed might the Blessed Lord come within the range of my eyes?
Or when will the highest good consisting in hearing his words be attained? // 16
Alas, woe unto me, who have committed offenses, who am devoid of success in religious rites,
far from Nārāyaṇa's grace, and within the grasp of the afflictions of saṃsāra! // 17
Bharadvāja said:
When the king was thus troubled with anxiety and indifferent to life,
Keśava, his form invisible, spoke while all were listening: // 18
The Blessed Lord said:

2.1.s: madekaśaraṇaṃ sādhuṃ tvāṃ tyakṣyāmi kathaṃ nṛpa .. 19 ..
2.1.d: मदेकशरणं साधुं त्वां त्यक्ष्यामि कथं नृप .. 19 ..
2.1.m: How could I abandon you, a virtuous man who have made me your sole refuge, O king? // 19
This mountain named Veṅkaṭa is renowned in the three worlds;
even more than Vaikuṇṭha, O king, it is an abode that brings me supreme joy. // 20

2.1.s: taṃ gatvā bhūdharavaraṃ tava bhaktyā tapasyataḥ ..
2.1.d: तं गत्वा भूधरवरं तव भक्त्या तपस्यतः ..
2.1.m: Having gone to that best of mountains, as you perform austerity with devotion,
when a thousand years have passed, I shall become visible [to you]. // 21
Agastya, zealous like you for my darśana, straightway
asked the Four-faced One: 'Where may Viṣṇu be seen?' // 22
'Hari can be seen on Mount Vṛṣabha by those who are self-restrained;
go there!'—thus the Lotus-born One said to the sage. // 23
Having been thus instructed by the lotus-born [Brahmā], the pot-born [Agastya]
will come to Añjanādri, that great abode, to perform austerity.
You too, having taken up residence on that sacred mountain,
intent on austerity and having worshipped me, will attain my darśana.
Now, the arrival of King Śaṅkha at the sacred Veṅkaṭācala by the Lord's instruction:
Bharadvāja said:
Thus commanded by the Lord, the enemy of the Dānavas,
Śaṅkha felt incomparable joy, thinking in his heart: “I am blessed!”
Having entrusted his son Vajra with the duty of protecting the subjects,
he went to the Nārāyaṇa mountain, yearning for the darśana of Govinda.
On its lofty peak he saw the auspicious Svāmipuṣkariṇī,
filled with divine waters resembling nectar,
frequented by hosts of numerous Siddhas, Gandharvas, and celestial seers,
soothing the distress of worldly existence, the refuge of all sacred fords,
abounding with cormorants, herons, curlews, swans, and kāraṇḍava ducks,
and delightful with white water-lilies, blue lotuses, pink lotuses, and fragrant water-lilies.

2.1.s: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā padminīṃ divyāṃ tattīre vihitoṭajaḥ ..
2.1.d: तां दृष्ट्वा पद्मिनीं दिव्यां तत्तीरे विहितोटजः ..
2.1.m: Having seen that divine lotus pool, he constructed a hut on its shore;
gratified by ritual ablutions, drinking, and other acts, with an unswerving focus of mind,
dedicating all actions to Janārdana, the Lord of the Universe.
Now, the arrival of Agastya at Veṅkaṭācala for the sake of the Lord's darśana:
Devoted constantly to japa and meditation, he performed very severe austerity.
At that very time, by the command of the Supreme Lord [Brahmā],
the sage Agastya too, surrounded by hundreds of sages, reached the primeval mountain.
Having begun from the western quarter, making an effort in circumambulation,
he wandered on the mountain for a long time, beholding the sacred fords.
There and then he saw those eager for the darśana of Hari:
Viriñci, Guha, Śakra, Īśa, Viṣvaksena, and others in succession,
the foremost yogins headed by Sanaka, and the seers headed by Nārada,
as well as Siddhas, Gandharvas, Daiteyas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and Pannagas.
Honored by each of them with humble and affectionate words,
he traversed about, beholding all the wondrous things.
Having bathed in all the sacred fords, such as Skandadhārā and others,
he worshipped Govinda, the Lord of the worlds, in each of those places.
As he thus wandered, when a thousand years had passed, that best of sages,
not having seen the lotus-eyed Lord, became filled with anxious grief.
Now, the speech of Guru, the Vasus, and others to Agastya:
At that time, Dhiṣaṇa and Uśanas, and again
the king Vasu, named Uparicara, approached that lord of seers: [41]
“O best of sages, our life has become fruitful,
since you have been seen by us, like a second Nārāyaṇa!
O sage, what we, intent on seeing Acyuta, were instructed
by Brahmā, the lord of the world, that is now told to you:
‘In the southern quarter there is a mountain named Veṅkaṭa,
which is an abode favored by Hari even above Śvetadvīpa.
On that mountain, Govinda, the teacher of the universe, will show his own form
to Agastya and to King Śaṅkha.
At that time, to all the gods, seers, Yakṣas, and Rakṣases,
and to us, darśana of the God of gods will occur.
That will happen before long; therefore, having abandoned all sins,
go to search for Agastya on that mountain of Nārāyaṇa!’
Thus commanded by the Creator, having arrived here by good fortune,
we have seen you, the highly fortunate one of immense splendor.
Having gone along with you to the bank of the Svāmipuṣkariṇī,
we shall also behold Śaṅkha, that foremost of the Lord's devotees.”
Now, the viewing of the delightful sights on the sacred Veṅkaṭācala by Agastya and others:
Bharadvāja said:
Thus instructed by the foremost ones headed by the Lord of Speech [Bṛhaspati],

2.1.s: śokajālaṃ parityajya yayau taiḥ sahito drutam .. 2.1.37.50 ..
2.1.d: शोकजालं परित्यज्य ययौ तैः सहितो द्रुतम् .. 2.1.37.50 ..
2.1.m: the pot-born [Agastya] cast off his web of grief and departed swiftly along with them.
He beheld great trees bowed down under the weight of fruits and flowers,
covering the horizons with the shade of their abundant, well-grown branches.
Lions, elephants, tigers, boars, buffaloes, and the like,
and beasts he observed along the path at various intervals. / (52)
Then they beheld peaks of the mountain,
adorned here and there with gold, silver, copper, and other [metals]. / (53)
Driving away gods by their spray and showers of flying drops,
uprooting boulders by their speed, hundreds of mountain torrents were seen. / (54)
A gentle breeze brought them delight,
carrying the fragrance of lotuses as it wandered over the mountain slopes. / (55)

2.1.s: śukānāṃ kokilānāṃ ca tadā śuśruvire giraḥ .. 56 ..
2.1.d: शुकानां कोकिलानां च तदा शुश्रुविरे गिरः .. 56 ..
2.1.m: Then the calls of parrots and cuckoos were heard. / (56)
Sitting here and there on broad rocks,
they saw siddhas singing of Kṛṣṇa's majestic virtues. / (57)
Walking around, all the lordly sages headed by Agastya
beheld the divine Svāmipuṣkariṇī with its pure waters. / (58)
[Agastya] saw King Śaṅkha, who had made his dwelling on its bank,
standing with his actions of speech, mind, and body concentrated on Hari. / (59)
Beholding those lords of sages of strict vows, he quickly
performed worship according to the injunctions, preceded by prostrations and praises. / (60)
Seated there, they all honoured one another with eagerness;
devoted to the praise of Govinda, they attained fulfillment. / (61)

2.1.m: Thus ends the thirty-seventh chapter, entitled 'The Description of the Arrival of Śaṅkha, Agastya, and Others at Mount Veṅkaṭa,' in the praise of the Suvarṇamukharīmāhātmya, in the Veṅkaṭācalamāhātmya, in the second section, the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, in the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. / (37)
Now, the manifestation of the Lord, pleased with the austerity of Agastya, Śaṅkha, and others.
Bharadvāja said:
For them whose minds were fixed upon Hari, the Lord of the universe,
devoted wholly to worship and praise, three days passed there. / (1)

2.1.s: tṛtīye divase prāpte te sarve nidritā niśi ..
2.1.d: तृतीये दिवसे प्राप्ते ते सर्वे निद्रिता निशि ..
2.1.m: When the third day arrived, they all fell asleep at night,
and at the end of the fourth watch they saw an excellent dream. / (2)
Puruṣottama, holding conch, discus, and mace in hand, gracious,
arrived to grant a boon, with smiling eyes, they beheld. / (3)
Rising with joyful hearts and coming forth from their dwelling,
they bathed duly and with devotion in the pure waters of Svāmipuṣkariṇī. / (4)
Having duly performed every rite appropriate for daybreak,
they returned to their dwelling to worship the god Acyuta. / (5)
On the way, an omen indicated by birds that brought immediate blessing,

2.1.s: dṛṣṭvā prasādaṃ devasya karasthaṃ menire tadā .. 6 ..
2.1.d: दृष्ट्वा प्रसादं देवस्य करस्थं मेनिरे तदा .. 6 ..
2.1.m: they saw, and considered the grace of the god already within their hands. / (6)
Then, having worshipped Janārdana, the maker of the three worlds,
they praised him with various holy hymns proclaimed in the Vedas. / (7)
At the conclusion of the praise, O son of Kuntī, the chief of sages born from a pot,
together with Śaṅkha, chanted the eight-syllabled mantra of Hari. / (8)
While their minds were thus offered to Acyuta, the Lord of the world,
before them appeared a single, wondrously great light, / (9)
as if a mass of radiance of many crores of suns, moons, and fires
had united and stood in the vault of heaven. / (10)
Beholding that light, all of them, moved by boundless wonder,
meditated on divine Nārāyaṇa, whose form is supreme bliss, / (11)
beyond the path of speech and mind, radiant with renowned sovereign power,
having a thousand eyes, endowed with thousands of arms and feet, / (12)
delightful with flashing splendour like molten gold,
terrifying with fangs, difficult to look upon, spewing masses of fire, / (13)
resplendent with the Kaustubha jewel, bearing Śrī upon his chest,
inconceivable, without beginning or end, inspiring immense terror, / (14)
illuminating the entire universe within himself, all-pervading.
Those [sages] headed by Agastya and Śaṅkha, with joyful hearts, / (15)
seeing that Lord of the universe, bowed down again and again.
Then the weapons of Hari, roaming for the protection of the worlds, / (16)
endowed with their own brilliance and strength, came to attend upon him:
the discus shining like the sun, the divine mace, the sword Nandaka, / (17)
the lotus, and Pāñcajanya of terrible sound, lustrous like the moon.
Then, overwhelmingly, it filled the entire cosmic egg— / (18)
the roar of Pāñcajanya, terrifying to all asuras.
Hearing the sound of Pāñcajanya, exceedingly wondrous and dreadful, / (19)
All the deities arrived, each mounted upon their own vehicle:
Brahmā, Rudra, Śatamakha, and Sanaka and the other yogins,
the sages headed by Vasiṣṭha, gandharvas, uragas, and kinnaras,
Viṣvaksena, Garuḍa, and Viṣṇu's attendants headed by Jaya,
and those eternal beings of equal form who dwell in Śvetadvīpa.
A wondrous rain of blossoms, born from celestial trees,
fell, delighting all minds with its dense fragrance.
Celestial fair-eyed women danced, foremost kinnaras sang,
and gods, gandharvas, and cāraṇas, trembling with joy, sang praises.
Seeing the lotus-eyed Lord gracious and affectionate to his devotees,
they bowed down with eight-limbed prostrations and gratified him with various hymns of praise.
Brahmā and the others said:
Victory to you, Viṣṇu, ocean of mercy! Victory, O lotus-eyed one!
Victory, sole granter of boons to the worlds! Victory, destroyer of the distress of devotees!
Endless, imperishable, tranquil, beyond the range of speech and mind—
who indeed knows you, whose nature consists of consciousness and bliss?
Subtler than the subtle, grosser than the gross, dwelling within all,
they declare you to be the infallible Person beyond material nature.
You whose nature is the essence of Vedānta, who exist inside and outside everything—

2.1.d: को हि वर्णयितुं शक्तो मायायत्तेषु देहिषु .. 29 ..
2.1.m: who indeed among embodied beings subjected to illusion is capable of describing you?
Having seen this form of yours that strikes great terror,

2.1.m: we are all agitated with fear; please assume a peaceful form!

and with a voice like the rumbling of a cloud respectfully said:
Now, the manner in which the Lord assumed a gentle form at the request of Brahmā and the others.
The Blessed Lord said:
Relinquishing this terrifying form, I shall assume

2.1.d: शान्तं रूपं भजिष्यामि मां पश्यत निराकुलाः .. 32 ..
2.1.m: a peaceful form that brings delight; look upon me, free from agitation!
Having spoken thus, having disappeared at that very moment,
he became pleasant to behold within an aerial chariot inlaid with gems.
His face like the orb of the moon, tranquil, with the luster of a blue lotus petal,
clad in golden-hued garments, adorned with jeweled ornaments,
his four hands shining with the conch, discus, mace, and lotus.
Beholding him, the beloved of Ramā, they bowed again and again.
Having satisfied Brahmā and the others by granting their desired wishes,
he spoke to Agastya, the foremost among sages, who was bowed with modesty:
The Blessed Lord said:
O best of sages, through severe vows performed toward me just now,
you are exhausted; I will grant you your desired boons, speak!
Bharadvāja said:

2.1.s: niśamya vākyaṃ śrībhartuḥ praṇamya ca punaḥpunaḥ ..
2.1.d: निशम्य वाक्यं श्रीभर्तुः प्रणम्य च पुनःपुनः ..
2.1.m: Hearing the words of Śrī's husband and bowing again and again,
the pot-born sage, with all his limbs thrilled with horripilation, spoke these words:
Now, the river Svarṇamukharī's attainment of supremacy over all, like the Lord himself, at the request of Agastya.
Agastya said:
Whatever has been offered in sacrifice, whatever austerity performed, whatever studied, whatever heard by me,
all that has borne fruit, since I have been honored by you.
I alone am truly righteous in all the three worlds, O Lord,
in that you have come in search of me who was now searching for you!
By your grace, all my desires were attained long ago;

2.1.s: na paśyāmi vicintyāpi prāpyaṃ saṃprati mādhava .. 41 ..
2.1.d: न पश्यामि विचिन्त्यापि प्राप्यं संप्रति माधव .. 41 ..
2.1.m: even upon reflection, I see nothing to be attained now, O Mādhava.
Nevertheless, out of fickleness, this is petitioned of you, O Lord:
make my devotion to your lotus feet constantly like this!
And consider this: at the request of the gods, by me
the river Suvarṇamukharī, which destroys a multitude of sins of those who bathe in it,
has arrived near the slopes of your mountain;
make her fulfilled, O Lord of the worlds, by your gracious favors!
Having bathed in the waters of the Suvarṇamukharī, those who behold [you]
standing on Veṅkaṭa—may they become vessels of enjoyment and liberation!
Short-lived men are foolish and fallen away from the yoga of knowledge;
[Short-lived, foolish men, fallen away from knowledge and yoga,] / cannot see you by rites of vows and study. (46)
Always abiding on this mountain, O Teacher of the Universe,
graciously disposed to all, O God, become the granter of desired ends! (47)
The Blessed Lord said:
What has been prayed for by you, O brahmin, that shall indeed be so;

2.1.s: nūnamapratimā loke mayi bhaktiḥ kṛtā tvayā .. 48 ..
2.1.d: नूनमप्रतिमा लोके मयि भक्तिः कृता त्वया .. 48 ..
2.1.m: truly, incomparable devotion to me has been offered by you in this world. (48)
Like the Jāhnavī, this river Suvarṇamukharī, O sage,
shall be longed for by the gods, bestowing desired fortune. (49)
And this Svāmipuṣkariṇī, endowed with bodily form as a river,
shall enter into that divine river, the resort of a multitude of tīrthas. (50)
On this mountain named Vaikuṇṭha, from this day forth, forever,
I shall dwell, O sage, by your prayer. (51)
Those who have washed away the mire of masses of sins by bathing in the Suvarṇamukharī,
and with composed minds behold me on this Vaikuṇṭha mountain— (52)
endowed with sons and other blessings on earth, possessing all sovereign power,
and after dying and enjoying pleasures in heaven until the end of the kalpa, (53)
free from rebirth, shining with pure bliss,
they shall reach my abode; no doubt should be entertained here. (54)
Welcoming all who come to see me with auspicious desires,
I shall constantly fulfill them, O sage, out of respect for your word. (55)
To those desiring sons, [I shall give] many sons; and wealth to those desiring wealth;
likewise, to those desiring health, a great relief from disease; (56)
likewise, the warding off of calamity for those overwhelmed by fierce misfortunes:
I will always bestow desired pleasures, even those difficult to attain. (57)
Whatever desires people hope for as they come here and behold me,
all of them obtain those very desires; of this there is no doubt. (58)

2.1.m: I am pleased by your devotion, O Śaṅkha! Choose a desired boon;
I, the giver of boons, give [it] to you who are emaciated and performing tapas. (61)
Śaṅkha said:
I ask for nothing else, O mighty-armed one, than service to your lotus feet;

The Blessed Lord said:
What has been prayed for by you, O Śaṅkha, that shall indeed be so;
what is unobtainable for those suited to the practice of my service? (63)
Staying in Indra's world until the end of the kalpa, served by hosts of apsarases,
and enjoying various pleasures, you shall then go to my realm. (64)

Nārāyaṇa, the origin of the universe, a wish-fulfilling tree to those who worship him. (65)

Lord, praised with devotion by those who meditate on him, vanished right there. (66)

Bharadvāja said:
This greatness of Mount Veṅkaṭa has been told to you, O Arjuna;

2.1.m: To her as she spoke thus, Mataṅga, the best of sages, replied:
"Hear my words, O lady, which bestow sons and grandsons.
To the south from here, at a distance of ten yojanas,
is the abode of Nṛsiṃha known as Ghanācala.
Upon it, fortunate lady, is the charming Brahmatīrtha.
And to the east of that, at a distance of just ten yojanas,
flows the river Suvarṇamukharī, foremost among rivers.
To the north of it lies the mountain named Vṛṣabhācala.
In front of it is an auspicious lake named Svāmipuṣkariṇī.

2.1.m: Thus addressed, the lady Añjanā, bowing down to him again and again,

Having bathed, bowed down to Varāha, and paid homage to Veṅkaṭeśa,
remembering the words of the seer Mataṅga again and again,
sweet-spoken Añjanā quickly went to Viyadgaṅgā.

2.1.m: Having bathed and drunk the auspicious water, turned toward its bank,
she performed austerity with restrained vows, directing it toward the breath-wind.
Subsisting on fruits, subsisting on water, and thereafter taking no food at all,

Her auspicious companion named Vipulā attended upon her.
And at the end of the thousand years, the wise god Vāyu,
the great-minded one, then appeared, speaking to her,
when the sun reached its entry into Aries, O best of sages,
on the holy lunar day called the full moon, conjoined with the constellation Citrā:
"I will grant your desire; choose a boon, O faithful observer of vows."

Having heard the words of the seer Mataṅga with a pure mind, (4)

and the sacred fords beginning with the Gaṅgā in the three worlds arrive here. (6)
There is no sacred ford in the cosmic egg equal to Mount Veṅkaṭa;
even there, the auspicious Svāmipuṣkariṇī is exceedingly meritorious. (7)

Those who arrive for ritual ablution when joined with the constellation Citrā, (8)

Whatever gifts should be made on Mount Veṅkaṭa, the best of mountains,

Now the praise of the gifts to be given on Mount Veṅkaṭācala as declared by Vyāsa:
Vyāsa said:
The gift of food and the gift of clothing—these two are extolled;
especially the funeral rites for a father, on Mount Veṅkaṭa, the best of mountains. (13)
Those who give gold for the pleasure of the Slayer of Madhu,
having reached every world, rejoice, O best of sages. (14)
Those who make a gift of a śālagrāma stone on this best of mountains,
their limbs suffer no injury, and they attain experience of the Self. (15)

2.1.m: He who gives the gift of a cow to an eminent brahmin who has a household,
shines in the world of Viṣṇu for a number of years equal to its hairs. (16)

2.1.m: He who gives land, O goddess, to a brahmin householder,

2.1.m: He who gives a maiden [in marriage], O goddess, to a brahmin learned in the Vedas,

Fragrances, campaka flowers and the like, umbrellas, fans, and chowries,
betel leaves, camphor, and the like—he who gives [these] to a twice-born (22)

2.1.m: enjoys pleasure for a long time, and then goes to heaven;
and having enjoyed manifold pleasures for a thousand divine years, (23)

2.1.s: sārvabhaumastato bhūtvā tatra bhuktvā ciraṃ mahīm ..
